deduped_items.title: СК проверит информацию о неоказании медпомощи участнику СВО в Ессентуках
deduped_items.body_text:
Краткий пересказ от РИА ИИ
- Следователи проверяют информацию о ненадлежащем оказании медицинской помощи участнику СВО в Ессентуках.
- Родственники участника СВО заявили, что Ессентукская больница дважды отказала в госпитализации мужчины с двойным инсультом.
- Краевой минздрав утверждает, что пациенту оказывается медицинская помощь в полном объеме в соответствии с действующими стандартами.
ЕССЕНТУКИ, 23 сен – РИА Новости. Следователи проверяют информацию о ненадлежащем оказании медицинской помощи участнику СВО в Ессентуках, сообщило СУСК РФ по Ставропольскому краю. 
Ранее местное издание "КМВ РУ" опубликовало материал со ссылкой на родственников участника СВО, которые заявили, что Ессентукская больница дважды отказалась в госпитализации мужчины с двойным инсультом. 
"По данному факту в следственном отделе по городу Ессентуки следственного управления Следственного комитета Российской Федерации по Ставропольскому краю незамедлительно организована процессуальная проверка по признакам преступления, предусмотренного ч. 2 ст. 124 УК РФ (неоказание помощи больному)", - сообщило ведомство в своем Telegram-канале. 
По данным СК, следователи устанавливают все обстоятельства произошедшего, ход и результаты проверки находятся на контроле регионального управления. 
При этом в краевом минздраве РИА новости сообщили, что пациенту в полном объеме оказывается медицинская помощь в соответствии с действующими стандартами.

deduped_items.title: Rupnik victims complain to pope on 'silences' over trial
deduped_items.summary: First letter to Leo: Covering up works at Lourdes was courageous act, but enough reticence
deduped_items.body_text:
Five alleged sex-abuse victims of
world-famous Slovenian mosaic artist and ex-Jesuit priest Marko
Rupnik wrote to Pope Leo XIV Wednesday complaining about
allegedly excessive silences covering his trial saying that this
was a further and continued violence against them.
                                    
                                       
				"We decided to write to you on the occasion of your trip to
France—and specifically your visit to Lourdes, where you will
meet abuse victims like us—at a site where Father Rupnik's
mosaics will no longer be visible on the basilica's façade,
following the decision to cover them permanently. It is a
powerful and courageous gesture that we greatly appreciated,"
the five alleged victims wrote in their first open letter to the
Pope, released by their lawyer Laura Sgrò; in it, however, they
also lament the excessive "silence" surrounding the proceedings
against the former Jesuit, describing it as "further and ongoing
violence" for them.
                                    
                                       
				The victims are are Slovenian women who are former members of
the Ignatius of Loyola Community of which the 71-year-old Rupnik
was a prominent member before being expelled five years ago.
                                    
                                       
				A Vatican court found Rupnik guilty of multiple rape.

world-famous Slovenian mosaic artist and ex-Jesuit priest Marko
Rupnik wrote to Pope Leo XIV Wednesday complaining about
allegedly excessive silences covering his trial saying that this
was a further and continued violence against them.

France—and specifically your visit to Lourdes, where you will
meet abuse victims like us—at a site where Father Rupnik's
mosaics will no longer be visible on the basilica's façade,
following the decision to cover them permanently. It is a
powerful and courageous gesture that we greatly appreciated,"
the five alleged victims wrote in their first open letter to the
Pope, released by their lawyer Laura Sgrò; in it, however, they
also lament the excessive "silence" surrounding the proceedings
against the former Jesuit, describing it as "further and ongoing
violence" for them.

the Ignatius of Loyola Community of which the 71-year-old Rupnik
was a prominent member before being expelled five years ago.
                                    
                                       
				A Vatican court found Rupnik guilty of multiple rape.

deduped_items.title: Sfida il robot sul ring, poi arriva il calcio: l’umanoide lo scaraventa a terra
deduped_items.summary: L'influencer Frankie LaPenna entra nella gabbia e prova a colpire l’umanoide, che incassa e risponde con una serie di calci fino a mandarlo a terra. La sfida si è svolta il 18 settembre a San Francisco ed è stata organizzata da REK, Robot Entertainment Kombat, che l’ha presentata come il primo combattimento tra una persona e un robot umanoide. LaPenna, contrariamente a quanto riportato in alcune ricostruzioni, è un creator statunitense. Il dettaglio decisivo: il robot non combatteva autonomament

deduped_items.body_text:
Los Juegos Deportivos de Escuelas Católicas de Madrid buscan nuevos árbitros para la temporada 2026-2027
Desde el Departamento de Deportes ya han convocado los cursos de formación arbitral para la XXXVIII edición de una competición que arranca el día 14 de noviembre
Madrid
La XXXVIII edición de los Juegos Deportivos de Escuelas Católicas de Madrid ya está aquí y desde el Departamento deDeporte Escolar y Valores se encuentran inmersos en la preparación de la temporada 2026-2027 que arrancará el sábado 14 de noviembre con ... la disputa de la primera jornada. Pero para que la competición pueda comenzar, es necesario que los árbitros den el pitido inicial. Por este motivo, desde la organización ya han abierto el plazo de inscripción para los cursos de formación arbitral, totalmente gratuitos y con prácticas en situaciones reales, para conformar al colectivo que dirigirá los encuentros de esta temporada.
El fin de semana del 2, 3 y 4 de octubre, Noelia Gutiérrez, árbitra Internacional FIFA y de Segunda división de fútbol sala, será la encargada de impartir el curso de este deporte y contará con la asistencia de Javier Esteban, director del Departamento y ex árbitro de Primera División. Por otro lado, los días 16, 17 y 18 de octubre tendrá lugar el curso de voleibol, cuyo profesor será Javier Rivero, responsable de competición. Para terminar la formación teórica, el curso para los noveles de baloncesto será impartido el mismo fin de semana por Carlos Gómez, coordinador de árbitros.
Además, el viernes 23 de octubre tendrá lugar la formación administrativa de todos los deportes y el sábado 24 se celebrarán los partidos correspondientes a la formación práctica, cuya asistencia es obligatoria para aquellas personas que aprueben la parte teórica. Las instalaciones del colegio Sagrado Corazón de Chamartín albergarán una mañana deportiva en la que los aspirantes podrán vivir su primera experiencia con el silbato en la mano.
«La liga de Escuelas Católicas es ideal para iniciarse en el mundo del arbitraje debido al trato personalizado y a los valores inherentes de la competición. Por este motivo, animo a todas las personas que quieran comenzar su andadura en el mundo del arbitraje a que se inscriban en nuestros cursos que, además, son totalmente gratuitos. deduped_items.body_text:
Los Juegos Deportivos de Escuelas Católicas de Madrid buscan nuevos árbitros para la temporada 2026-2027
Desde el Departamento de Deportes ya han convocado los cursos de formación arbitral para la XXXVIII edición de una competición que arranca el día 14 de noviembre
Madrid
La XXXVIII edición de los Juegos Deportivos de Escuelas Católicas de Madrid ya está aquí y desde el Departamento deDeporte Escolar y Valores se encuentran inmersos en la preparación de la temporada 2026-2027 que arrancará el sábado 14 de noviembre con ... la disputa de la primera jornada. Pero para que la competición pueda comenzar, es necesario que los árbitros den el pitido inicial. Por este motivo, desde la organización ya han abierto el plazo de inscripción para los cursos de formación arbitral, totalmente gratuitos y con prácticas en situaciones reales, para conformar al colectivo que dirigirá los encuentros de esta temporada.
El fin de semana del 2, 3 y 4 de octubre, Noelia Gutiérrez, árbitra Internacional FIFA y de Segunda división de fútbol sala, será la encargada de impartir el curso de este deporte y contará con la asistencia de Javier Esteban, director del Departamento y ex árbitro de Primera División. Por otro lado, los días 16, 17 y 18 de octubre tendrá lugar el curso de voleibol, cuyo profesor será Javier Rivero, responsable de competición. Para terminar la formación teórica, el curso para los noveles de baloncesto será impartido el mismo fin de semana por Carlos Gómez, coordinador de árbitros.
Además, el viernes 23 de octubre tendrá lugar la formación administrativa de todos los deportes y el sábado 24 se celebrarán los partidos correspondientes a la formación práctica, cuya asistencia es obligatoria para aquellas personas que aprueben la parte teórica. Las instalaciones del colegio Sagrado Corazón de Chamartín albergarán una mañana deportiva en la que los aspirantes podrán vivir su primera experiencia con el silbato en la mano.
«La liga de Escuelas Católicas es ideal para iniciarse en el mundo del arbitraje debido al trato personalizado y a los valores inherentes de la competición. Por este motivo, animo a todas las personas que quieran comenzar su andadura en el mundo del arbitraje a que se inscriban en nuestros cursos que, además, son totalmente gratuitos. También quiero agradecer a los árbitros veteranos que cada año renuevan su compromiso y nos ayudan a equilibrar la balanza entre árbitros jóvenes y árbitros experimentados» asegura Carlos Gómez coordinador de árbitros del Departamento de Deporte Escolar y Valores.
Como es habitual, la inscripción es gratuita. Los interesados en asistir a los cursos deberán aporten tres kilos de comida no perecedera para colaborar con el Banco de Alimentos de Madrid o una entidad similar. La información completa, así como el formulario de inscripción, se encuentra en la web de la competición.
Para los árbitros veteranos, el Departamento ha decidido continuar con la campaña el 'árbitro amigo'. Esta iniciativa consiste en bonificar a aquellos árbitros y/o centros que aporten un árbitro para al menos 17 del total de las jornadas programadas. «Cada persona que venga de tu parte y pite toda la temporada hará que ganes 15 euros», reza el lema de la campaña. Además, los candidatos que vengan de parte de algún centro escolar harán ganar a su institución 30 euros.
AVANCE PARA LA TEMPORADA 2026/2027
El plazo de inscripción de equipos para la temporada 2026-2027 ya está abierto y se cerrará el día 22 de octubre. Por otro lado, la competición arrancará el segundo fin de semana del mes de noviembre, pero durante este mes y el que viene son varias las fechas que cabe destacar. El próximo miércoles, día 23 de septiembre, tendrá lugar la reunión de coordinadores deportivos a las 18.00 horas en formato online. En dicha reunión se tratarán los cambios en las Bases de Competición, los cambios en la Normativa General y las nuevas reglas de baloncesto, fútbol sala y voleibol.
El miércoles 7 de octubre tendrá lugar una reunión

deduped_items.title: Court overturns large fines against misleading education firms over missing screenshots
deduped_items.summary: Thirteen educational institutions accused of misleading students about the degree they could obtain will not have to pay about 450,000 euros in fines, as investigators handling the case failed to t
deduped_items.body_text:
Court overturns large fines against misleading education firms over missing screenshots
Thirteen educational institutions accused of misleading students about the degree they could obtain will not have to pay about 450,000 euros in fines, as investigators handling the case failed to take screenshots of websites and marketing material which could have proved the allegations. The highest administrative court in the Netherlands dismissed the penalties on appeal in a ruling published on Wednesday.
It has not been proven that the institutions involved conferred titles on their students without approval from the Accreditation Organisation of the Netherlands and Flanders (NVAO), according to the verdict from the Council of State's court branch. Further, there was no evidence submitted which demonstrated that the institutions made false claims.
The Council of State did not state which educational institutions were involved, however it appeared likely that the matter was linked to a 2022 report from the Education Inspectorate taking the adult education firm NCOI to task for offering programs using terms like "master," "professional master," or "executive master". Since then, the NCOI Group has been organized as the Salta Group.
"Based on the findings" in the report, "the Inspectorate concludes that between September 2017 and June 2021, the institution wrongfully awarded 435 degrees for professional master's and executive master's programs for which no NVAO accreditation existed," the Inspectorate wrote. This was in violation of the Higher Education Act," the report stated. The specific number of 435 degrees was also referenced in the lower court ruling that was appealed to the Council of State.
A master's title is a protected term, and only accredited institutions may award them. However, such words do not automatically make it a "master's degree" under the law, the Council of State ruled. It added that it is also not a criminal offense for others to get the impression that their training did lead to a master's title.
The institutions took the matter to the District Court for The Hague, which ruled in favor of the minister. They then lodged an appeal with the Council of State, the highest administrative court. The Council said that the inspectorate "failed to substantiate the findings with evidence." As a result, the minister "did not concretely and specifically record what was wrong and what has been improved," according to the Council.
The institutions were initially ordered to pay a combined total of approximately 470,000 euros. Former Education Minister Robbert Dijkgraaf imposed these fines two years after the Inspectorate's initial report, which determined that the situation had not sufficiently improved, and students still were not receiving clear information.
On June 26, 2023, the Ministry of Education issued fines against the institutions LOI, NCOI, NTI, Luzac, Scheidegger, Schoevers, SRM, Bestuursacademie Nederland, Tio, Pro Education, Boertien Vergouwen Overduin, ISBW, and Markus Verbeek Praehep. The highest fine, initially 207,250 euros, was for NCOI. This amount was later reduced to 194,000 euros.
Reporting by ANP and NL Times

deduped_items.title: Family demands investigation into Rotterdam woman's death after Aruba rollover crash
deduped_items.summary: The family of a 23-year-old Rotterdam woman who died on the island of Aruba earlier this month is calling for further investigation into the circumstances surrounding the off-road vehicle crash tha
deduped_items.body_text:
Family demands investigation into Rotterdam woman's death after Aruba rollover crash
The family of a 23-year-old Rotterdam woman who died on the island of Aruba earlier this month is calling for further investigation into the circumstances surrounding the off-road vehicle crash that caused her death. Kimberly van Ardenne was with her boyfriend on holiday, visiting their friend, a Dutch Marine who lives there. All three were in the utility terrain vehicle when it rolled over near Grapefield, an area with rocky cliffs and a beach in San Nicolas at the southern end of the island.
Within hours of the crash, officers responding to the scene had identified Van Ardenne as the driver. In a statement posted to social media, Aruba police wrote that they first learned of the crash a few minutes before 3 p.m. that Sunday afternoon.
"On arrival it was found that a UTV had somehow overturned, and the driver appeared to be in grave condition," police said. Despite paramedics' efforts, the Rotterdam woman was pronounced dead at the scene by a forensic doctor. In the same statement, police said she was the driver, confirming a statement from her boyfriend, who was not seriously injured.
However, witnesses have painted a different picture in comments on social media, and in remarks to media outlets. One person claimed they saw the trio tearing up the area around Carnival Village about three kilometers west of the crash site. They left after 15 minutes, and Van Ardenne was not behind the wheel of the off-road vehicle, which rolled over soon after, according to 24ora.
"We would very much like to know exactly what happened," her surviving family members wrote in a public appeal. "We have heard various accounts, but we also know there were actual witnesses at the scene of the accident. We appeal to anyone who was present or has information to contact us," they wrote.
What is clear is that all three people were in the vehicle at the time of the incident, and their friend was responsible for arranging the off-road vehicle, according to RTL. The family said some pieces simply do not add up.
Van Ardenne did not enjoy driving in general, nor and was especially cautious. She was not the type to drive any vehicle dangerously, especially not in the wild manner seen at Carnival Village, according to her cousin, Stephanie, who spoke to RTL on the family's behalf.
The case will now be investigated by the Marechaussee, a spokesperson told the broadcaster. The branch of the military typically handles inquiries where military personnel were involved may have acted wrongfully.
Van Ardenne's body was repatriated to the Netherlands, and her family has been meeting with people this week who wanted to offer support. Her funeral was scheduled to take place this Saturday in Rotterdam.
"With deep sorrow, we must say goodbye far too soon to our daughter, granddaughter, sister, niece, and friend," the family stated. "We will carry her warmth, love, and unique personality in our hearts forever."

deduped_items.summary: The case relates to the Polish National Foundation, a body created under the former government to promote Poland abroad.
deduped_items.body_text:

Agents from Poland’s Central Anti-Corruption Bureau (CBA) have detained a senior official from opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki’s chancellery as part of a probe into alleged misspending of funds under the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government.
An employee of a major right-wing broadcaster, Republika, was also taken into custody as part of the same investigation, which relates to the activities of the Polish National Foundation (PFN), a body created under the PiS government to promote Poland abroad but which was also used to further the party’s political interests.
Dzisiaj rano w Warszawie na polecenie Prokuratury Regionalnej w Rzeszowie agenci @CBAgovPL zatrzymali Piotra M. i Annę P.
▶️ Zatrzymane osoby przewożone są do @Prok_Regio_RZE, która prowadzi śledztwo dotyczące nieprawidłowości w Polskiej Fundacji Narodowej.
▶️ Na tym etapie…
— Jacek Dobrzyński (@JacekDobrzynski) September 23, 2026
On Tuesday morning, Jacek Dobrzyński, the spokesman for the security services, announced that two individuals, named only as Piotr M. and Anna P. under Polish privacy law, had been detained by the CBA at the request of prosecutors investigating irregularities in the PFN.
Both suspects previously worked in the chancellery of Prime Minister Beata Szydło, who was head of the PiS government from 2015 to 2017. Piotr M. was head of the Government Information Centre (CIR) and Anna P. led the media services department.
Anna P. now works for Nawrocki, who was elected as president last year with the support of PiS. She is director of the Presidential Events Office, which organises the president’s schedule. Piotr M. currently works as a commentator for Republika, a station generally supportive of Nawrocki and PiS.
Agenci CBA zatrzymali w Warszawie Piotra M. i Annę P. Sprawa dotyczy nieprawidłowości w Polskiej Fundacji Narodowej! pic.twitter.com/e3jw3ekdOA
— Iwona Hartwich (@iwonahartwich) September 23, 2026
In 2017, while still working in Szydło’s chancellery, Piotr M. and Anna P. founded a PR company called Solvere. Later that same year, the company was hired to run a prominent and controversial campaign for the PFN called “Fair Courts”, receiving a reported 1.2 million zloty (€275,000) for the project.
The PFN had been set up the previous year under Szydło’s government with funding from 17 state-owned companies. Its publicly declared and statutory mission was to promote Poland abroad.
However, the “Fair Courts” campaign, which cost around 8.4 million zloty, was run in Poland itself, with material in Polish, and aimed to show the alleged failings of the justice system in Poland in order to justify why controversial reforms being implemented by PiS were necessary.
Echoing PiS rhetoric, the campaign suggested that judges saw themselves as a “special caste” and highlighted cases of alleged wrongdoing by individual judges, including one who had been caught stealing a sausage. (The judge in question had not ruled on a case since that incident in 2006 and had died in 2015.)
In 2018, a Warsaw court ruled that the “Fair Courts” campaign was inconsistent with the PFN’s statutory goals, saying that not only did the adverts fail to enhance Poland’s image abroad, “on the contrary, they significantly weakened it, creating a negative image of the judiciary based on individual cases”.
In February 2025, just over a year after PiS lost power, a newly appointed PFN board accused its predecessors of criminal negligence that caused damages of over 30 million zloty to the foundation’s finances. They notified prosecutors of potential crimes.

Agents from Poland’s Central Anti-Corruption Bureau (CBA) have detained a senior official from opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki’s chancellery as part of a probe into alleged misspending of funds under the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government.
An employee of a major right-wing broadcaster, Republika, was also taken into custody as part of the same investigation, which relates to the activities of the Polish National Foundation (PFN), a body created under the PiS government to promote Poland abroad but which was also used to further the party’s political interests.
Dzisiaj rano w Warszawie na polecenie Prokuratury Regionalnej w Rzeszowie agenci @CBAgovPL zatrzymali Piotra M. i Annę P.
▶️ Zatrzymane osoby przewożone są do @Prok_Regio_RZE, która prowadzi śledztwo dotyczące nieprawidłowości w Polskiej Fundacji Narodowej.
▶️ Na tym etapie…
— Jacek Dobrzyński (@JacekDobrzynski) September 23, 2026
On Tuesday morning, Jacek Dobrzyński, the spokesman for the security services, announced that two individuals, named only as Piotr M. and Anna P. under Polish privacy law, had been detained by the CBA at the request of prosecutors investigating irregularities in the PFN.
Both suspects previously worked in the chancellery of Prime Minister Beata Szydło, who was head of the PiS government from 2015 to 2017. Piotr M. was head of the Government Information Centre (CIR) and Anna P. led the media services department.
Anna P. now works for Nawrocki, who was elected as president last year with the support of PiS. She is director of the Presidential Events Office, which organises the president’s schedule. Piotr M. currently works as a commentator for Republika, a station generally supportive of Nawrocki and PiS.
Agenci CBA zatrzymali w Warszawie Piotra M. i Annę P. Sprawa dotyczy nieprawidłowości w Polskiej Fundacji Narodowej! pic.twitter.com/e3jw3ekdOA
— Iwona Hartwich (@iwonahartwich) September 23, 2026
In 2017, while still working in Szydło’s chancellery, Piotr M. and Anna P. founded a PR company called Solvere. Later that same year, the company was hired to run a prominent and controversial campaign for the PFN called “Fair Courts”, receiving a reported 1.2 million zloty (€275,000) for the project.
The PFN had been set up the previous year under Szydło’s government with funding from 17 state-owned companies. Its publicly declared and statutory mission was to promote Poland abroad.
However, the “Fair Courts” campaign, which cost around 8.4 million zloty, was run in Poland itself, with material in Polish, and aimed to show the alleged failings of the justice system in Poland in order to justify why controversial reforms being implemented by PiS were necessary.
Echoing PiS rhetoric, the campaign suggested that judges saw themselves as a “special caste” and highlighted cases of alleged wrongdoing by individual judges, including one who had been caught stealing a sausage. (The judge in question had not ruled on a case since that incident in 2006 and had died in 2015.)
In 2018, a Warsaw court ruled that the “Fair Courts” campaign was inconsistent with the PFN’s statutory goals, saying that not only did the adverts fail to enhance Poland’s image abroad, “on the contrary, they significantly weakened it, creating a negative image of the judiciary based on individual cases”.
In February 2025, just over a year after PiS lost power, a newly appointed PFN board accused its predecessors of criminal negligence that caused damages of over 30 million zloty to the foundation’s finances. They notified prosecutors of potential crimes.

▶️ Zatrzymane osoby przewożone są do @Prok_Regio_RZE, która prowadzi śledztwo dotyczące nieprawidłowości w Polskiej Fundacji Narodowej.
▶️ Na tym etapie…
— Jacek Dobrzyński (@JacekDobrzynski) September 23, 2026
On Tuesday morning, Jacek Dobrzyński, the spokesman for the security services, announced that two individuals, named only as Piotr M. and Anna P. under Polish privacy law, had been detained by the CBA at the request of prosecutors investigating irregularities in the PFN.
Both suspects previously worked in the chancellery of Prime Minister Beata Szydło, who was head of the PiS government from 2015 to 2017. Piotr M. was head of the Government Information Centre (CIR) and Anna P. led the media services department.
Anna P. now works for Nawrocki, who was elected as president last year with the support of PiS. She is director of the Presidential Events Office, which organises the president’s schedule. Piotr M. currently works as a commentator for Republika, a station generally supportive of Nawrocki and PiS.
Agenci CBA zatrzymali w Warszawie Piotra M. i Annę P. Sprawa dotyczy nieprawidłowości w Polskiej Fundacji Narodowej! pic.twitter.com/e3jw3ekdOA
— Iwona Hartwich (@iwonahartwich) September 23, 2026
In 2017, while still working in Szydło’s chancellery, Piotr M. and Anna P. founded a PR company called Solvere. Later that same year, the company was hired to run a prominent and controversial campaign for the PFN called “Fair Courts”, receiving a reported 1.2 million zloty (€275,000) for the project.
The PFN had been set up the previous year under Szydło’s government with funding from 17 state-owned companies. Its publicly declared and statutory mission was to promote Poland abroad.
However, the “Fair Courts” campaign, which cost around 8.4 million zloty, was run in Poland itself, with material in Polish, and aimed to show the alleged failings of the justice system in Poland in order to justify why controversial reforms being implemented by PiS were necessary.
Echoing PiS rhetoric, the campaign suggested that judges saw themselves as a “special caste” and highlighted cases of alleged wrongdoing by individual judges, including one who had been caught stealing a sausage. (The judge in question had not ruled on a case since that incident in 2006 and had died in 2015.)
In 2018, a Warsaw court ruled that the “Fair Courts” campaign was inconsistent with the PFN’s statutory goals, saying that not only did the adverts fail to enhance Poland’s image abroad, “on the contrary, they significantly weakened it, creating a negative image of the judiciary based on individual cases”.
In February 2025, just over a year after PiS lost power, a newly appointed PFN board accused its predecessors of criminal negligence that caused damages of over 30 million zloty to the foundation’s finances. They notified prosecutors of potential crimes.

deduped_items.title: Three Nobel Laureates Join Initiative for Laser-Based Early Disease Detection
deduped_items.summary: The Center for Molecular Fingerprinting (CMF) is strengthening its scientific leadership with three new Nobel laureates joining its advisory board. Simultaneously, the institute is expanding its pioneering laser-based early diagnosis project into Asia. Budapest-based CMF, led by Nobel laureate Ferenc Krausz, has expanded its scientific advisory board with three new members: cell biologist Randy Schekman, […] The post Three Nobel Laureates Join Initiative for Laser-Based Early Disease Detection a
deduped_items.body_text:
The aim is to develop a cost-effective testing method that will enable the early detection of diseases.Continue reading
The Center for Molecular Fingerprinting (CMF) is strengthening its scientific leadership with three new Nobel laureates joining its advisory board. Simultaneously, the institute is expanding its pioneering laser-based early diagnosis project into Asia.
Budapest-based CMF, led by Nobel laureate Ferenc Krausz, has expanded its scientific advisory board with three new members: cell biologist Randy Schekman, pharmacologist Louis J. Ignarro, and laser physicist Donna Strickland. Alongside earlier appointee Steven Chu, these five Nobel laureates will now shape the institute’s strategic direction.
CMF’s goal is to establish preventive, personalized medicine capable of detecting serious diseases such as cancer or type 2 diabetes even before the first clinical symptoms appear.
Conventional medical diagnostics often only come into play when symptoms are present or laboratory values deviate from broad population averages. The Center for Molecular Fingerprinting takes a different approach. Instead of a rigid average, the individual’s unique molecular baseline serves as the reference value.
Even minimal, patient-specific deviations in the blood can indicate early-stage pathological processes. To make these minute nuances visible, the institute uses a highly complex laser-optical method:
- Sample collection: Plasma is separated from the blood of study participants.
- Laser excitation: Ultrashort laser pulses excite the molecules contained in the plasma, causing them to vibrate. The process can be compared to striking a tuning fork and analyzing its decaying tone—with the difference that, instead of sound waves, molecular vibrations are detected using specialized optics.
- Molecular fingerprint: The overall pattern of these vibrations yields an individual molecular profile that documents even the slightest biochemical shifts.
Currently, 13,000 volunteers are contributing to the research through regular blood donations as part of the H4H program.
Marking the announcement, Sun Dong, Minister of Innovation, Technology and Industry for the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, and Péter Horváth, Hungarian State Secretary for Science and Innovation, toured CMF’s laboratory facilities in Szeged. During the visit, Ferenc Krausz showcased newly commissioned cryogenic storage units designed to ensure the integrity of blood samples.
The institute is now scaling up its research internationally through a strategic partnership with the University of Hong Kong.
Participant recruitment and the establishment of an Asian biobank are now underway in Hong Kong, running parallel to the Hungarian study cohorts.
Péter Horváth emphasized on site that the years of preparatory work are now nearing the stage of evaluating concrete data sets. If the hypotheses are confirmed, the government intends to continue supporting the project consistently and roll it out more broadly.
Behind the initiative lies a structural transformation—both economic and societal. Modern healthcare systems are largely designed to provide curative care for existing conditions—often through lengthy, invasive, and costly therapies.
Effective early detection, on the other hand, enables timely interventions, lifestyle adjustments, and targeted therapies in the early stages.
For Nobel laureate Louis Ignarro, the project marks the logical next step in modern medicine. Identifying early biomolecular abnormalities requires a shift in thinking to fully decipher the biological relevance of the subtlest signaling patterns. Steven Chu also sees the potential for a paradigm shift in this approach. “Today, it is no longer necessary to wait until an abnormality falls outside the normal range of the population average. This is precisely what can revolutionize diagnostics,” he explained.
Featured image: CMF

Conventional medical diagnostics often only come into play when symptoms are present or laboratory values deviate from broad population averages. The Center for Molecular Fingerprinting takes a different approach. Instead of a rigid average, the individual’s unique molecular baseline serves as the reference value.
Even minimal, patient-specific deviations in the blood can indicate early-stage pathological processes. To make these minute nuances visible, the institute uses a highly complex laser-optical method:
- Sample collection: Plasma is separated from the blood of study participants.
- Laser excitation: Ultrashort laser pulses excite the molecules contained in the plasma, causing them to vibrate. The process can be compared to striking a tuning fork and analyzing its decaying tone—with the difference that, instead of sound waves, molecular vibrations are detected using specialized optics.
- Molecular fingerprint: The overall pattern of these vibrations yields an individual molecular profile that documents even the slightest biochemical shifts.
Currently, 13,000 volunteers are contributing to the research through regular blood donations as part of the H4H program.
Marking the announcement, Sun Dong, Minister of Innovation, Technology and Industry for the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, and Péter Horváth, Hungarian State Secretary for Science and Innovation, toured CMF’s laboratory facilities in Szeged. During the visit, Ferenc Krausz showcased newly commissioned cryogenic storage units designed to ensure the integrity of blood samples.
The institute is now scaling up its research internationally through a strategic partnership with the University of Hong Kong.
Participant recruitment and the establishment of an Asian biobank are now underway in Hong Kong, running parallel to the Hungarian study cohorts.
Péter Horváth emphasized on site that the years of preparatory work are now nearing the stage of evaluating concrete data sets. If the hypotheses are confirmed, the government intends to continue supporting the project consistently and roll it out more broadly.
Behind the initiative lies a structural transformation—both economic and societal. Modern healthcare systems are largely designed to provide curative care for existing conditions—often through lengthy, invasive, and costly therapies.
Effective early detection, on the other hand, enables timely interventions, lifestyle adjustments, and targeted therapies in the early stages.
For Nobel laureate Louis Ignarro, the project marks the logical next step in modern medicine. Identifying early biomolecular abnormalities requires a shift in thinking to fully decipher the biological relevance of the subtlest signaling patterns. Steven Chu also sees the potential for a paradigm shift in this approach. “Today, it is no longer necessary to wait until an abnormality falls outside the normal range of the population average. This is precisely what can revolutionize diagnostics,” he explained.

deduped_items.body_text:
Czech Man Jailed 13 Days After Protest on Moscow's Red Square
Prague Morning
A judge at Moscow’s Tverskoy District Court sentenced a Czech man to 13 days in jail on Tuesday for staging a protest on Red Square.
Identified as Michal Plamenek, the man was arrested for holding up a sign in English next to Lenin’s Mausoleum on Sunday afternoon, the court’s press service said in a statement.
No details were provided as to what was written on Plamenek’s sign, but the court press service said a judge ruled that the inscription was “aimed at discrediting the Russian Armed Forces.”
Police officers arrested Plamenek because Red Square directly adjoins the Kremlin, where protests are banned. He allegedly refused to listen to a request by officers to accompany them to a police station and resisted arrest.
A judge found Plamenek guilty on three separate administrative counts of discrediting the Russian military, violating protest rules and disobeying a police officer.

deduped_items.body_text:
Heating Season Starts Across Czechia as Temperatures Fall
Prague Morning
District heating plants across the Czech Republic are beginning to supply heat as temperatures drop, with conditions for the start of the heating season now being met in much of the country.
Some plants have already begun providing additional heat during the colder morning and evening hours. The first systems to respond were mainly in mountainous parts of northern and western Czechia and in the Vysočina region.
Other heating plants are expected to gradually start operating in the coming days, depending on local temperatures and weather forecasts.
Since 2010, district heating systems have generally started supplying heat after September 20, although the exact timing varies considerably from year to year.
If temperatures rise again in late September or early October, heating can be suspended. Under the standard rules, heating is normally interrupted when the average outdoor temperature exceeds 13°C for two consecutive days and the forecast indicates that temperatures will continue to rise.
Last winter was colder than average
The previous heating season placed greater demands on heating systems than the years immediately before it.
According to figures from the Czech District Heating Association, the season was 4.9 percent colder than the previous year. It was also 3.2 percent colder than the average of the preceding 15 years.
The colder conditions translated into higher demand for heat, particularly during periods of sustained low temperatures.
Heating costs could increase next year
Households are not currently expected to face a direct increase resulting from a recent change in the interpretation of a fuel tax exemption, but some other users of district heating could see higher costs.
The issue concerns combined heat and power (CHP) generation. This year, the state changed how an existing fuel tax exemption is interpreted, limiting its application to the amount of heat supplied to households.
Heating companies say the change could increase annual heating bills for institutions such as hospitals and schools by tens or even hundreds of thousands of Czech crowns.

deduped_items.title: Supreme Court: Finnish police's forcible removals of hijabs from women was lawful
deduped_items.summary: The long-running legal case dates back to an incident at a police station in Hämeenlinna in May 2017, and the verdict has been seen as potentially setting a precedent for future cases.
deduped_items.body_text:
Finland's Supreme Court has upheld a ruling by the Court of Appeal, which found that police officers were justified in their actions when they forcibly removed hijab headscarves from two female asylum seekers.
The Supreme Court's ruling is especially relevant because it has been viewed as potentially setting a precedent for any similar cases in the future.
The long-running case relates to an incident at a police station in Hämeenlinna in May 2017.
Police officers were required to take registration photos of the two women in order to process their asylum applications, and instructed them to remove their head coverings. Both women however refused, citing their religious beliefs.
According to the Finnish Police Board's guidelines for the taking of such photos, if a person is wearing a "headscarf or veil" which is related to their religious beliefs, the photos must be taken both with and without the covering.
Because of this guideline, an inspector at the station ordered his officers to remove the women's scarves, by force if necessary.
As a result of the incident, the police officers and security guards — comprising seven defendants in total — were later charged with assault, incitement to assault and breach of duty.
Kanta-Häme District Court dismissed the charges in September 2022, and that verdict was upheld by the court of appeal in 2024.
In its decision, the appeals court ruled that the officers had no reason not to comply with the Finnish Police Board's policy that existed at the time, and they therefore were ruled to have not committed any offence.
The Supreme Court's latest ruling confirms this interpretation of the law.
The court noted that the police's necessity to photograph the women without headscarves was based on an acceptable societal objective — the proper processing of an asylum application and verification of an applicant's identity.
The court however also emphasised that force should only be used as a "last resort measure" in such situations and only if "advice, requests, and orders" have not been sufficient.

deduped_items.title: DNA of body in Enggano Bengkulu matches Arupadatu crew member: Police
deduped_items.summary: The Banten Regional Police confirmed that DNA test results have identified a body found on Enggano Island, Bengkulu, as ...
deduped_items.body_text:
The boat was carrying a group of journalists when it lost contact in the waters of the Sunda Strait off Pandeglang, Banten, on September 7.
Banten Regional Police Chief Inspector General Hengki said the identification was confirmed after the Disaster Victim Identification (DVI) team conducted a thorough examination and matched DNA data.
“DNA examination of the body found on Enggano Island identified the individual as Sukarman, a crew member and the biological father of Yayan,” he said at a press conference on Wednesday.
Hengki explained that the identification was part of the SAR operation for eight people — five journalists and three crew members of the speedboat — who lost contact after departing from Pagedongan Carita Pier in Pandeglang at 2 p.m. local time to cover the eruption of Mount Anak Krakatau.
After 10 days of intensive searches by a joint team, a breakthrough came on September 12 when Bengkulu police officers discovered an unidentified male body in the waters of Sawang Bengkok, Kahyapu Village, Enggano Subdistrict.
Following the discovery, the Banten Regional Police's Medical and Health Division coordinated with the local police to secure the body and transport it by Cessna aircraft to Bhayangkara Hospital in Bengkulu for further identification.
“The authorities then submitted antemortem and postmortem data on the eight missing victims. The team conducted data matching by analyzing fingerprints, dental records, and DNA samples,” Hengki said.
Following the identification, Sukarman’s body is scheduled to be flown from Bengkulu to Soekarno-Hatta International Airport in Tangerang before being transported to his home in Pandeglang.
“The body will be transported tomorrow from Bengkulu to Soekarno-Hatta Airport, after which it will be handed over to the family,” Hengki said.
Related news: SAR team ends 10-day search for missing journalists in Sunda Strait
Related news: ANTARA mourns missing photojournalist as 10-day SAR search ends
Translator: Azmi Syamsul M, Resinta Sulistiyandari

The boat was carrying a group of journalists when it lost contact in the waters of the Sunda Strait off Pandeglang, Banten, on September 7.
Banten Regional Police Chief Inspector General Hengki said the identification was confirmed after the Disaster Victim Identification (DVI) team conducted a thorough examination and matched DNA data.
“DNA examination of the body found on Enggano Island identified the individual as Sukarman, a crew member and the biological father of Yayan,” he said at a press conference on Wednesday.
Hengki explained that the identification was part of the SAR operation for eight people — five journalists and three crew members of the speedboat — who lost contact after departing from Pagedongan Carita Pier in Pandeglang at 2 p.m. local time to cover the eruption of Mount Anak Krakatau.
After 10 days of intensive searches by a joint team, a breakthrough came on September 12 when Bengkulu police officers discovered an unidentified male body in the waters of Sawang Bengkok, Kahyapu Village, Enggano Subdistrict.
Following the discovery, the Banten Regional Police's Medical and Health Division coordinated with the local police to secure the body and transport it by Cessna aircraft to Bhayangkara Hospital in Bengkulu for further identification.
“The authorities then submitted antemortem and postmortem data on the eight missing victims. The team conducted data matching by analyzing fingerprints, dental records, and DNA samples,” Hengki said.
Following the identification, Sukarman’s body is scheduled to be flown from Bengkulu to Soekarno-Hatta International Airport in Tangerang before being transported to his home in Pandeglang.
“The body will be transported tomorrow from Bengkulu to Soekarno-Hatta Airport, after which it will be handed over to the family,” Hengki said.

deduped_items.title: COA flags OVP over relief operations, documentation lapses
deduped_items.summary: In its consolidated audit report on the country's disaster risk reduction and management funds, state auditors reported that the OVP’s relief operations suffered from inconsistent reporting, unauthorized operational deviations, “issuance of open-ended mission orders,” and incomplete documentation.
deduped_items.body_text:
COA flags OVP over relief operations, documentation lapses
MANILA, Philippines — The Commission on Audit (COA) has flagged the Sara Duterte-led Office of the Vice President (OVP) over a series of control and documentation deficiencies in its disaster relief operations, raising concerns over the reliability and verifiability of its distribution records.
In its consolidated audit report on the country's disaster risk reduction and management funds for calendar year 2025, state auditors reported that the OVP’s relief operations suffered from inconsistent reporting, unauthorized operational deviations, “issuance of open-ended mission orders,” and incomplete documentation.
“Control and documentation deficiencies were observed in the implementation of Relief Operations, such as: (a) inconsistencies between Situational Report (SitReps) from the agencies/LGUs concerned and Office of the Vice President (OVP) SitReps; (b) deviations from approved Mission Orders during actual operations; (c) issuance of open-ended Mission Orders; (d) deficiencies in beneficiary documentation and distribution records; and (e) incomplete, missing, or non-submission of required documents, contrary to Section 9.0 of the Policy Manual on Disaster Operations Program dated June 26, 2024 and Section G of OVP Office Order No. 2025-74. These deficiencies reduced assurance on the completeness, reliability, and verifiability of relief distribution records and weakened controls over Relief Operations. (OVP).”
State auditors discovered significant discrepancies between the Situational Reports (SitReps) prepared by local government units or affected agencies and those drafted by the OVP. These inconsistencies involved welfare goods valued at P19.67 million.
The COA noted differences in the reported number of affected families, while some local reports completely lacked beneficiary counts.
“Although management attributed these to evolving disaster conditions and subsequent validation, supporting documents for the revisions were not consistently attached. Consequently, the reliability of the SitReps used as basis for planning relief operations and issuing Mission Orders was diminished,” the COA’s report read.
The COA also called out the OVP for deviating from its own approved Mission Orders during actual field deployments.
State auditors identified 24 relief operations, involving P39,009,054.98 worth of welfare goods, that altered schedules, distribution sites, and the volume of relief items and rice without securing documented approvals.
“The deviations included changes in schedules, distribution locations, quantities of relief items, and the amount of rice distributed. While management cited operational adjustments due to changing field conditions, the absence of documented approvals weakened assurance that the changes were properly authorized and supported,” the COA said.
Furthermore, the OVP issued eight open-ended Mission Orders for distributions totaling P84.12 million. Because these orders failed to specify target beneficiaries, auditors noted that the OVP lacked a concrete basis for determining the exact quantity of goods requested and distributed.
The audit further exposed widespread deficiencies in beneficiary documentation and distribution records.
State auditors also flagged uncertified Master Lists, unsigned Relief Distribution Sheets (RDS), duplicate entries, and incomplete beneficiary information.
In 11 relief operations involving more than 200 beneficiaries, the OVP inappropriately applied documentary requirements meant for individual crises rather than the procedures mandated by its Disaster Operations Policy Manual, leading to inconsistent practices and a lack of verifiability.
Compounding these issues, relief operations serving 33,980 beneficiaries and utilizing P25.27 million in welfare goods completely lacked vital pre-operation documents, such as verified Master Lists and SitReps.

deduped_items.summary: In its consolidated audit report on the country's disaster risk reduction and management funds, state auditors reported that the OVP’s relief operations suffered from inconsistent reporting, unauthorized operational deviations, “issuance of open-ended mission orders,” and incomplete documentation.
deduped_items.body_text:
COA flags OVP over relief operations, documentation lapses
MANILA, Philippines — The Commission on Audit (COA) has flagged the Sara Duterte-led Office of the Vice President (OVP) over a series of control and documentation deficiencies in its disaster relief operations, raising concerns over the reliability and verifiability of its distribution records.
In its consolidated audit report on the country's disaster risk reduction and management funds for calendar year 2025, state auditors reported that the OVP’s relief operations suffered from inconsistent reporting, unauthorized operational deviations, “issuance of open-ended mission orders,” and incomplete documentation.
“Control and documentation deficiencies were observed in the implementation of Relief Operations, such as: (a) inconsistencies between Situational Report (SitReps) from the agencies/LGUs concerned and Office of the Vice President (OVP) SitReps; (b) deviations from approved Mission Orders during actual operations; (c) issuance of open-ended Mission Orders; (d) deficiencies in beneficiary documentation and distribution records; and (e) incomplete, missing, or non-submission of required documents, contrary to Section 9.0 of the Policy Manual on Disaster Operations Program dated June 26, 2024 and Section G of OVP Office Order No. 2025-74. These deficiencies reduced assurance on the completeness, reliability, and verifiability of relief distribution records and weakened controls over Relief Operations. (OVP).”
State auditors discovered significant discrepancies between the Situational Reports (SitReps) prepared by local government units or affected agencies and those drafted by the OVP. These inconsistencies involved welfare goods valued at P19.67 million.
The COA noted differences in the reported number of affected families, while some local reports completely lacked beneficiary counts.
“Although management attributed these to evolving disaster conditions and subsequent validation, supporting documents for the revisions were not consistently attached. Consequently, the reliability of the SitReps used as basis for planning relief operations and issuing Mission Orders was diminished,” the COA’s report read.
The COA also called out the OVP for deviating from its own approved Mission Orders during actual field deployments.
State auditors identified 24 relief operations, involving P39,009,054.98 worth of welfare goods, that altered schedules, distribution sites, and the volume of relief items and rice without securing documented approvals.
“The deviations included changes in schedules, distribution locations, quantities of relief items, and the amount of rice distributed. While management cited operational adjustments due to changing field conditions, the absence of documented approvals weakened assurance that the changes were properly authorized and supported,” the COA said.
Furthermore, the OVP issued eight open-ended Mission Orders for distributions totaling P84.12 million. Because these orders failed to specify target beneficiaries, auditors noted that the OVP lacked a concrete basis for determining the exact quantity of goods requested and distributed.
The audit further exposed widespread deficiencies in beneficiary documentation and distribution records.
State auditors also flagged uncertified Master Lists, unsigned Relief Distribution Sheets (RDS), duplicate entries, and incomplete beneficiary information.
In 11 relief operations involving more than 200 beneficiaries, the OVP inappropriately applied documentary requirements meant for individual crises rather than the procedures mandated by its Disaster Operations Policy Manual, leading to inconsistent practices and a lack of verifiability.
Compounding these issues, relief operations serving 33,980 beneficiaries and utilizing P25.27 million in welfare goods completely lacked vital pre-operation documents, such as verified Master Lists and SitReps.

deduped_items.title: Iran airlines suspend more international flights as US sanctions take effect
deduped_items.summary: TEHRAN, Sept 23 — Iranian airlines were forced to cancel some international flights on Wednesday after the US tigh...
deduped_items.body_text:
TEHRAN, Sept 23 — Iranian airlines were forced to cancel some international flights on Wednesday after the US tightened sanctions on Iran’s aviation industry in a new effort to cripple its economy.
A travel agent in Tehran told AFP that flights to Baghdad, Muscat, Qatar, Georgia and Azerbaijan had all been suspended, but routes to multiple other destinations remained available, including China.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced the new measures on Monday as part of an earlier threat to impose “economic D-Day” on Iran, an attempt to force it into submission following their nearly seven-month war.
But Iran’s aviation sector has already been a target of sanctions for years, and it remains unclear what the full impact will be and whether other countries will comply.
Even after the new sanctions took effect on Wednesday, a flight from Tehran operated by Mahan Air, one of Iran’s biggest carriers, landed in Guangzhou in China, according to tracking data from FlightRadar24.
China on Tuesday said it opposes the US sanctions and called them illegal. A flight to Shanghai was also due to depart on Wednesday, according to Tehran’s international airport.
Some flights to Istanbul were also scheduled, though others had been cancelled, the travel agent in Tehran told AFP.
“The situation is unstable and we are no longer selling tickets for the time being for fear of cancellations,” the the agent said, requesting anonymity.
A Mahan flight from Kabul was also expected to arrive in Tehran around midday. According to the website for Tehran’s international airport, other connections to Turkey and Armenia also remained possible using smaller Iranian airlines, including Varesh.
Flights to Najaf in Iraq and Dubai in the United Arab Emirates were also scheduled.
Bessent on Monday vowed to “shut down” Iranian carriers and punish anyone doing business with them.
“If they land, you cannot provide them with fuel, you cannot provide them with landing services, you cannot sell them tickets or you will be knocked out of the dollar system,” he warned other countries.
The restrictions will further complicate the ability of Iranians to travel abroad or return to their country.
Pilgrims
Iranian media also reported cancellations, with the Tasnim news agency on Tuesday citing a civil aviation spokesman as saying that Baghdad and Muscat airports “will no longer accept” Iranian flights.
“Other international flights, including Istanbul, will operate as scheduled and as usual, and at present there are no problems with these flights,” Tasnim said.
According to Tasnim, Iran’s aviation authorities are in talks to reroute Baghdad flights to Najaf, a major destination for Iranian pilgrims.
In Iraq, while the government has not publicly announced plans to enforce the ban, several sources including a senior government official told AFP that Baghdad would comply with the US measures.
The prospect of a suspension of flights between the two countries has sparked concerns from some Iraqi travel agents.
In Najaf, home to one of the most revered Shia Muslim shrines, agent Haidar Shamaa said “most travel companies in the city depend on booking flights” to Iranian airports.
Several travel agencies said panicked clients were calling for updates and were considering switching to land routes, which would mean much longer journeys. — AFP

deduped_items.title: Indonesia identifies body of missing Anak Krakatau crew member, seven including journalists remain missing
deduped_items.summary: JAKARTA, Sept 23 — Indonesian police have identified a body found in Bengkulu as crew member Surakman, one of eigh...
deduped_items.body_text:
JAKARTA, Sept 23 — Indonesian police have identified a body found in Bengkulu as crew member Surakman, one of eight people, including five journalists, who went missing while covering the Anak Krakatau eruption earlier this month.
Seven people remain missing.
Banten Police Chief Inspector General Hengki said Surakman’s body was found on Enggano Island in Bengkulu province on September 12.
“Based on the DNA examination, the body found on Enggano Island, Bengkulu, was genetically identified as Surakman, a crew member of the speedboat,” he told a press conference at the Banten Police headquarters in Serang on Wednesday, which was streamed live.
The eight were aboard a speedboat that departed Carita in Banten’s Pandeglang district at about 2pm on September 7 for waters near Anak Krakatau.
They were travelling to cover the volcano’s eruption when contact with the boat was lost later that day.
The five missing journalists are Muhammad Bagus Khoirunnas of Antara news agency, Firdaus Wajidi of Anadolu Ajansi, Arie Basuki of Merdeka.com, Yudistiro Pranoto of iNews and freelance journalist Donal Husni.
The two remaining crew members are Warta and Heriyanto. — Bernama

deduped_items.summary: The armed forces on Wednesday shot down eight drones launched by the Afghan Taliban after they entered Pakistani airspace near the Torkham border and Kohat, according to security sources. deduped_items.body_text:
The armed forces on Wednesday shot down eight drones launched by the Afghan Taliban after they entered Pakistani airspace near the Torkham border and Kohat, according to security sources.
The sources said the drones were intercepted by the air defence systems, which they described as “active and vigilant”.
“The armed forces and the ‘Shaheens’ of the Pakistan Air Force professionally thwarted the Afghan Taliban regime’s cowardly attempt to target public areas,” security sources said.
According to the sources, four of the eight drones were shot down in areas adjacent to the Torkham border, while the remaining four were downed near Kohat.
Earlier, security sources said two “rudimentary” drones had been brought down using “soft skill” methods about seven kilometres from Kohat city. They said the armed forces’ air defence systems remained on round-the-clock alert and were maintaining vigilance against “all threats from Kharjistan”.
“This incursion serves as yet another proof of the Afghan Taliban regime’s direct support and patronage of terrorists,” security sources said.
Later, security sources said the wreckage of the destroyed drones was being recovered. Last night’s exchange of fire in Kurram sector and Wednesday’s drone incursion “demonstrated the state of the Afghan Taliban’s panic and disarray,” security sources added.
The development comes two days after Pakistan, in response to recent terrorist attacks in KP, conducted “calibrated” airstrikes in the border region with Afghanistan against terrorist hideouts and safe havens of terrorist organisations.

deduped_items.title: Iran airlines suspend more international flights as US sanctions take effect
deduped_items.summary: TEHRAN, Sept 23 — Iranian airlines were forced to cancel some international flights on Wednesday after the US tigh...
deduped_items.body_text:
TEHRAN, Sept 23 — Iranian airlines were forced to cancel some international flights on Wednesday after the US tightened sanctions on Iran’s aviation industry in a new effort to cripple its economy.
A travel agent in Tehran told AFP that flights to Baghdad, Muscat, Qatar, Georgia and Azerbaijan had all been suspended, but routes to multiple other destinations remained available, including China.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced the new measures on Monday as part of an earlier threat to impose “economic D-Day” on Iran, an attempt to force it into submission following their nearly seven-month war.
But Iran’s aviation sector has already been a target of sanctions for years, and it remains unclear what the full impact will be and whether other countries will comply.
Even after the new sanctions took effect on Wednesday, a flight from Tehran operated by Mahan Air, one of Iran’s biggest carriers, landed in Guangzhou in China, according to tracking data from FlightRadar24.
China on Tuesday said it opposes the US sanctions and called them illegal. A flight to Shanghai was also due to depart on Wednesday, according to Tehran’s international airport.
Some flights to Istanbul were also scheduled, though others had been cancelled, the travel agent in Tehran told AFP.
“The situation is unstable and we are no longer selling tickets for the time being for fear of cancellations,” the the agent said, requesting anonymity.
A Mahan flight from Kabul was also expected to arrive in Tehran around midday. According to the website for Tehran’s international airport, other connections to Turkey and Armenia also remained possible using smaller Iranian airlines, including Varesh.
Flights to Najaf in Iraq and Dubai in the United Arab Emirates were also scheduled.
Bessent on Monday vowed to “shut down” Iranian carriers and punish anyone doing business with them.
“If they land, you cannot provide them with fuel, you cannot provide them with landing services, you cannot sell them tickets or you will be knocked out of the dollar system,” he warned other countries.
The restrictions will further complicate the ability of Iranians to travel abroad or return to their country.
Pilgrims
Iranian media also reported cancellations, with the Tasnim news agency on Tuesday citing a civil aviation spokesman as saying that Baghdad and Muscat airports “will no longer accept” Iranian flights.
“Other international flights, including Istanbul, will operate as scheduled and as usual, and at present there are no problems with these flights,” Tasnim said.
According to Tasnim, Iran’s aviation authorities are in talks to reroute Baghdad flights to Najaf, a major destination for Iranian pilgrims.
In Iraq, while the government has not publicly announced plans to enforce the ban, several sources including a senior government official told AFP that Baghdad would comply with the US measures.
The prospect of a suspension of flights between the two countries has sparked concerns from some Iraqi travel agents.
In Najaf, home to one of the most revered Shia Muslim shrines, agent Haidar Shamaa said “most travel companies in the city depend on booking flights” to Iranian airports.
Several travel agencies said panicked clients were calling for updates and were considering switching to land routes, which would mean much longer journeys. — AFP

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced the new measures on Monday as part of an earlier threat to impose “economic D-Day” on Iran, an attempt to force it into submission following their nearly seven-month war.
But Iran’s aviation sector has already been a target of sanctions for years, and it remains unclear what the full impact will be and whether other countries will comply.
Even after the new sanctions took effect on Wednesday, a flight from Tehran operated by Mahan Air, one of Iran’s biggest carriers, landed in Guangzhou in China, according to tracking data from FlightRadar24.
China on Tuesday said it opposes the US sanctions and called them illegal. A flight to Shanghai was also due to depart on Wednesday, according to Tehran’s international airport.
Some flights to Istanbul were also scheduled, though others had been cancelled, the travel agent in Tehran told AFP.
“The situation is unstable and we are no longer selling tickets for the time being for fear of cancellations,” the the agent said, requesting anonymity.
A Mahan flight from Kabul was also expected to arrive in Tehran around midday. According to the website for Tehran’s international airport, other connections to Turkey and Armenia also remained possible using smaller Iranian airlines, including Varesh.
Flights to Najaf in Iraq and Dubai in the United Arab Emirates were also scheduled.
Bessent on Monday vowed to “shut down” Iranian carriers and punish anyone doing business with them.
“If they land, you cannot provide them with fuel, you cannot provide them with landing services, you cannot sell them tickets or you will be knocked out of the dollar system,” he warned other countries.
The restrictions will further complicate the ability of Iranians to travel abroad or return to their country.
Pilgrims
Iranian media also reported cancellations, with the Tasnim news agency on Tuesday citing a civil aviation spokesman as saying that Baghdad and Muscat airports “will no longer accept” Iranian flights.
“Other international flights, including Istanbul, will operate as scheduled and as usual, and at present there are no problems with these flights,” Tasnim said.
According to Tasnim, Iran’s aviation authorities are in talks to reroute Baghdad flights to Najaf, a major destination for Iranian pilgrims.
In Iraq, while the government has not publicly announced plans to enforce the ban, several sources including a senior government official told AFP that Baghdad would comply with the US measures.
The prospect of a suspension of flights between the two countries has sparked concerns from some Iraqi travel agents.
In Najaf, home to one of the most revered Shia Muslim shrines, agent Haidar Shamaa said “most travel companies in the city depend on booking flights” to Iranian airports.
Several travel agencies said panicked clients were calling for updates and were considering switching to land routes, which would mean much longer journeys. — AFP

deduped_items.title: Iran airlines suspend more international flights as US sanctions take effect
deduped_items.summary: TEHRAN, Sept 23 — Iranian airlines were forced to cancel some international flights on Wednesday after the US tigh...
deduped_items.body_text:
TEHRAN, Sept 23 — Iranian airlines were forced to cancel some international flights on Wednesday after the US tightened sanctions on Iran’s aviation industry in a new effort to cripple its economy.
A travel agent in Tehran told AFP that flights to Baghdad, Muscat, Qatar, Georgia and Azerbaijan had all been suspended, but routes to multiple other destinations remained available, including China.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced the new measures on Monday as part of an earlier threat to impose “economic D-Day” on Iran, an attempt to force it into submission following their nearly seven-month war.
But Iran’s aviation sector has already been a target of sanctions for years, and it remains unclear what the full impact will be and whether other countries will comply.
Even after the new sanctions took effect on Wednesday, a flight from Tehran operated by Mahan Air, one of Iran’s biggest carriers, landed in Guangzhou in China, according to tracking data from FlightRadar24.
China on Tuesday said it opposes the US sanctions and called them illegal. A flight to Shanghai was also due to depart on Wednesday, according to Tehran’s international airport.
Some flights to Istanbul were also scheduled, though others had been cancelled, the travel agent in Tehran told AFP.
“The situation is unstable and we are no longer selling tickets for the time being for fear of cancellations,” the the agent said, requesting anonymity.
A Mahan flight from Kabul was also expected to arrive in Tehran around midday. According to the website for Tehran’s international airport, other connections to Turkey and Armenia also remained possible using smaller Iranian airlines, including Varesh.
Flights to Najaf in Iraq and Dubai in the United Arab Emirates were also scheduled.
Bessent on Monday vowed to “shut down” Iranian carriers and punish anyone doing business with them.
“If they land, you cannot provide them with fuel, you cannot provide them with landing services, you cannot sell them tickets or you will be knocked out of the dollar system,” he warned other countries.
The restrictions will further complicate the ability of Iranians to travel abroad or return to their country.
Pilgrims
Iranian media also reported cancellations, with the Tasnim news agency on Tuesday citing a civil aviation spokesman as saying that Baghdad and Muscat airports “will no longer accept” Iranian flights.
“Other international flights, including Istanbul, will operate as scheduled and as usual, and at present there are no problems with these flights,” Tasnim said.
According to Tasnim, Iran’s aviation authorities are in talks to reroute Baghdad flights to Najaf, a major destination for Iranian pilgrims.
In Iraq, while the government has not publicly announced plans to enforce the ban, several sources including a senior government official told AFP that Baghdad would comply with the US measures.
The prospect of a suspension of flights between the two countries has sparked concerns from some Iraqi travel agents.
In Najaf, home to one of the most revered Shia Muslim shrines, agent Haidar Shamaa said “most travel companies in the city depend on booking flights” to Iranian airports.
Several travel agencies said panicked clients were calling for updates and were considering switching to land routes, which would mean much longer journeys. — AFP

Ye said his decision to join Nanjing University and leave the University of Michigan was not influenced by the death of Chinese scholar Wang Danhao on the same campus six months earlier – a day after Wang was interviewed by US Homeland Security officers.
“This is a career choice and has no connection to the events mentioned in your email or the national policies [of the Trump administration],” Ye said in an email on Tuesday.
“I have indeed joined my alma mater, Nanjing University, to participate in the development of its school of life sciences.”

deduped_items.title: US stresses backing for Asian allies
deduped_items.body_text:

            US stresses backing for Asian alliesCALL: US, Japanese and South Korean foreign ministers expressed support for Taiwan’s meaningful participation in appropriate international organizations
  - Reuters, NEW YORK
 The US on Monday reiterated its commitment to the defense of key Asian allies Japan and South Korea, and the three nations expressed support for Taiwan ahead of a summit this week between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping (習近平). Analysts say the US allies are anxious that Trump might offer concessions to Xi including over Taiwan and trade in return for an economic win with Beijing when he hosts the Chinese president at the White House in Washington tomorrow. Officials say Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and South Korean President Lee Jae-myung are keen to see the US president during the UN General Assembly in New York, where all three were scheduled to speak yesterday. From left, South Korean Minister of Foreign Affairs Cho Hyun, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Japanese Minister of Foreign Affairs Toshimitsu Motegi pose for a photograph ahead of their talks in New York on Monday.Photo: EPA US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Monday met with his South Korean counterpart Cho Hyun and Japanese Minister of Foreign Affairs Toshimitsu Motegi in New York. They issued a joint statement vowing, in apparent reference to China, to stand firm “against economic coercion and non-market policies and practices” and “arbitrary export restrictions that disrupt supply chains.” They also welcomed the launch of a new trilateral consultation mechanism on economic security, part of broader efforts to strengthen supply chains and cooperation on critical technologies. The statement said the US “reiterated its ironclad commitments to the defense of Japan and the ROK [Republic of Korea], backed by America’s unmatched military strength, including its nuclear capabilities, and reaffirmed its extended deterrence commitments to Japan and the ROK,” referring to South Korea’s official name. Presidential Office spokeswoman Karen Kuo speaks at a news conference in an undated photograph.Photo: Taipei Times The statement said the ministers emphasized their commitment to robust security cooperation and the importance of maintaining peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait. It “expressed support for Taiwan’s meaningful participation in appropriate international organizations.” Referring to North Korea, the ministers “reaffirmed their resolute commitment to the complete denuclearization of the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea” and called on it to resume dialogue. In Taipei, Presidential Office spokeswoman Karen Kuo (郭雅慧) yesterday said that peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait and the broader region represent a firm global consensus and an essential pillar of world security and prosperity, directly impacting shared international interests. The Presidential Office welcomed and appreciated the three foreign ministers’ concrete actions demonstrating an unwavering commitment to regional stability, she added. Amid a rapidly shifting geopolitical landscape, democratic partners must stand together to uphold the rules-based international order, Kuo said. As a frontline defender of global democracy, Taiwan remains determined to maintain regional peace and stability as a responsible international actor, she said. “Peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait are not only critical to the security and prosperity of the Indo-Pacific, but also closely tied to the stability of the global economy and supply chains,” Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesman Hsiao Kuang-wei (蕭光偉) said separately yesterday. The US, Japan and South Korea’s reaffirmation of the significance of maintaining peace and stability in the Taiwan Strait fully demonstrates that security across the Strait has become a strong consensus within the international community, he said.
