deduped_items.title: Flu epidemic continues as deaths and cases hit new high
deduped_items.body_text:
- 
            Flu epidemic continues as deaths and cases hit new highAT-RISK GROUPS: Of the accumulated 1,586 severe cases and 304 related deaths in this flu season, 65.8% were older people and 83.2% had chronic diseases, an official said
  - By Lee I-chia / Staff reporter
 The Centers for Disease Control (CDC) yesterday said that 165 severe flu cases and 30 flu-related deaths were reported last week, the highest weekly numbers in this flu season, and that cases might continue to increase, urging people to take precautions. Medical visits for flu-like illnesses increased by 1.4 percent to 141,374 last week, with 11.8 percent being emergency visits, showing that the seasonal flu is still in its epidemic period, CDC Epidemic Intelligence Center Director Guo Hung-wei (郭宏偉) said. From Tuesday last week to Monday, 165 severe flu cases and 30 flu-related deaths were confirmed, the highest weekly numbers since October last year, and also the highest numbers of the same week in five years, he said. Centers for Disease Control Deputy Director-General Lin Ming-cheng, center, holds a news conference in Taipei yesterday.Photo: Hou Chia-yu, Taipei Times Of the accumulated 1,586 severe cases and 304 flu-related deaths in this flu season, 65.8 percent were people aged 65 or older, and 83.2 percent had chronic diseases, he said, adding that elderly people with underlying conditions have the highest risk of developing severe illness. Among the latest confirmed flu deaths, the youngest was a five-year-old boy who did not have underlying health conditions, but also did not get vaccinated, CDC physician Lin Yung-ching (林詠青) said. The boy began having flu-like symptoms late last month and first sought treatment at a clinic, but as he later developed recurring fever, altered consciousness and convulsions, he was referred to a hospital for emergency treatment, Lin said. At the hospital he was confirmed to be infected with influenza A virus and showed signs of encephalitis, he said. The boy remained unconscious for more than two weeks in an intensive care unit and died of influenza-induced acute necrotizing encephalopathy combined with sepsis, he said. Contact tracing found that a person living with the boy had also contracted the flu late last month, Lin said. Guo said medical visits for COVID-19 increased 20.6 percent to 14,462 last week, and 48 severe cases and nine deaths were confirmed from Tuesday last week to Monday. Among the deaths was a man in his 30s, who had multiple chronic health conditions, and he died of cardiogenic shock and septic shock about two weeks after hospitalization, Lin said. As transmittable respiratory diseases typically become more active when temperatures drop, the CDC urge people to practice hand and respiratory hygiene, he said. Infected high-risk people, including young children, people with chronic conditions and older people, should also seek medical attention as soon as possible, especially if they develop symptoms such as difficulty breathing and altered consciousness, he said. Flu cases are expected to rise to a peak of 150,000 to 160,000 weekly medical visits, CDC Deputy Director-General Lin Min-cheng (林明誠) said. There is an increased infection risk as people congregate during the upcoming Mid-Autumn Festival, Lin Min-cheng said. As for a cluster of 11 acute hepatitis C cases that was traced to a clinic in New Taipei City’s Banciao District (板橋), Lin said two new cases were confirmed last week among the 1,118 people who received injections from January to last month and were notified that they could get a free blood test. A total of 1,111 people has been informed by the local health department, and seven could not be reached, he said. Of the 418 people who have been contacted but have not received the free blood test, 36 refused to get tested, four had died, and 32 reported receiving a blood test on their own, he said, adding that the positivity rate of the tested people so far was 3.08 percent. deduped_items.title: Chiang, Shen neck-and-neck in Taipei, poll suggests
deduped_items.body_text:
- 
            Chiang, Shen neck-and-neck in Taipei, poll suggests
  - By Lin Che-yuan / Staff reporter
 A poll released yesterday suggested that Taipei Mayor Chiang Wan-an (蔣萬安) of the Chinese Nationalist Party (KMT) and Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) Legislator Puma Shen (沈伯洋) are neck-and-neck in the Taipei mayoral race. The poll asked Taipei residents: “With just more than two months remaining before the Taipei mayoral election, six candidates have reportedly registered to run. If the election were held now, who would you most likely vote for?” The results showed that 41.7 percent said they would vote for Chiang, 40.5 percent for Shen, 0.7 percent for Kuo Hsi (郭璽) of the Taiwan Mahjong Greatest Party, 0.6 percent for Tang Hsin-min (唐新民) of the Three Forces Unity Promotion Alliance, 0.5 percent for Hsiao Wen-chien (蕭文乾) of the MiLinguall Party and 0.3 percent for independent candidate Lin Chih-cheng (林志成). On the other hand, 5.2 percent said they would not vote or would cast an invalid ballot, while 10.6 percent gave no answer. Taipei Mayor Chiang Wan-an, front, second right, signs an autograph during a visit to a traditional market in Taipei’s Wanhua District yesterday.Photo: CNA Through cross-analysis, the results suggested people aged 50 or above tended to support Chiang, while those aged 20 to 49 tended to support Shen. In terms of political leaning, 96.1 percent of KMT supporters said they intended to vote for Chiang, compared with 88.5 percent of Taiwan People’s Party supporters, the poll showed. Meanwhile 89.4 percent of DPP supporters said they would vote for Shen. Democratic Progressive Party Legislator and Taipei mayoral candidate Puma Shen, center, high-fives with supporters at Yanshan Night Market in Taipei last night.Photo: Lo Pei-de, Taipei Times Among politically unaffiliated voters, 31.7 percent said they would back Chiang and 25.9 percent said they would vote for Shen, while 12.1 percent said they did not plan to vote and 27.4 percent remained undecided or declined to give an answer, the poll showed. A gender breakdown of the figures suggested male voters favored Shen at 43.3 percent to Chiang’s 41.0 percent, while Chiang held a decisive lead among female voters, capturing 42.3 percent support over Shen’s 38.1 percent, a 4.2 percentage-point margin. The poll was commissioned by the Taipei Trust in Democracy Association, designed and analyzed by polling expert Tai Li-an (戴立安), and conducted by Beacon Market Research from Wednesday to Friday last week. It surveyed 1,076 people aged 20 or older, with 752 interviews conducted via landline and 324 via mobile phone. It has a margin of error of 3.0 percentage points. Chiang yesterday said that “any numbers are merely for reference,” adding that the municipal team’s top priority remains steadily advancing city affairs. Shen expressed confidence in Tai’s long-established credibility. “If anyone wants to question the validity of a poll, they should simply present scientific evidence,” Shen said. “Slapping labels on it arbitrarily is meaningless. It is crucial that we stick to professional standards,” he said, referring to criticism over the association’s alleged ties to United Microelectronics Corp founder Robert Tsao (曹興誠), who had donated to the civil defense organization Kuma Academy founded by Shen and worked closely with Shen during the recall campaign against KMT lawmakers last year. Association founder and chairman Huang Ching-lung (黃清龍) yesterday said he cofounded the organization with like-minded friends, adding that the poll was directly commissioned and funded by the association. Tai said that having conducted polling for organizations across the political spectrum, the key lies in maintaining complete transparency by publicly disclosing the survey’s methodology, design and authorship. Neurobiologist Ye Bing says his return to China is not spurred by Michigan campus tragedy
Prominent researcher takes over Nanjing University’s school of life sciences, rejecting claims US policy prompted his return

Neurobiologist Ye Bing is returning to China after a long period in the United States, but he says his move is not linked to the suicide of another Chinese scholar at the same university or US policy under the Trump administration.
Ye said his decision to join Nanjing University and leave the University of Michigan was not influenced by the death of Chinese scholar Wang Danhao on the same campus six months earlier – a day after Wang was interviewed by US Homeland Security officers.
“This is a career choice and has no connection to the events mentioned in your email or the national policies [of the Trump administration],” Ye said in an email on Tuesday.
“I have indeed joined my alma mater, Nanjing University, to participate in the development of its school of life sciences.”

deduped_items.summary: North Korea’s 2026 constitutional amendment protecting Pyongyang Cultural Language has fueled a renewed puppet speech crackdown. Schools, workplaces and neighborhood organizations have stepped up enforcement. South Korean-influenced expressions such as “jagiya” (honey), “oppa” and “jjokpalrida” (embarrassing) are not treated as harmless slang. “Oppa” is a term South Korean women traditionally use for an older brother […]

deduped_items.title: A ‘grubby rumour’ and a $5m extortion attempt: former Toplace executive gives Icac evidence
deduped_items.summary: Sharangan Maheswaran also told inquiry his bid for story on unsubstantiated rumour about then-Liberal minister David Elliott was ‘not a serious offer’Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updatesGet our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcastA purported $5m extortion attempt of fugitive property developer Jean Nassif was actually a genuine request for his company Toplace to pay a contractor, a lawyer assisting the New South Wales anti-corruption watchdog has argued.Former To
deduped_items.body_text:
A purported $5m extortion attempt of fugitive property developer Jean Nassif was actually a genuine request for his company Toplace to pay a contractor, a lawyer assisting the New South Wales anti-corruption watchdog has argued.
Former Toplace lawyer and executive Sharangan Maheswaran told the Independent Commission Against Corruption (Icac) on Wednesday he had not “dishonestly conveyed” to the building commissioner, David Chandler, that someone had attempted to extort Nassif on Chandler’s behalf.
Icac is investigating the allegation that Liberal figures Christian Ellis, Jeremy Greenwood and Charles Perrottet took $2m in illegal donations from Nassif or Toplace in exchange for political outcomes.
Greenwood and Perrottet have denied payments were for political outcomes. Ellis has moved overseas and is not expected to give evidence. Nassif, in an appearance from his Beirut bedroom, insisted he was “not corrupt”. Maheswaran, who is named in a separate allegation by Icac, has denied any wrongdoing.
The alleged outcomes include damage to the political career of Liberal minister, David Elliott, who had opposed Toplace developments, and the removal of the building commissioner, David Chandler, who had been scrutinising defects in Toplace apartments.
The commission has previously heard that Nassif claimed two individuals had asked him for $5m on Chandler’s behalf to lift prohibition orders on Toplace developments. Maheswaran subsequently passed on details of the alleged extortion attempt to Charles Perrottet.
Chandler is not named as a person of interest in Icac’s allegations and is not accused of any wrongdoing.
On Wednesday, the commission heard a phone call recorded by Nassif with one of the alleged individuals, contractor Navid Ardestani, who is not named in Icac’s allegations and is not accused of any wrongdoing.
“Navid mate,” Nassif began the call. “I didn’t know you were so fucking powerful, mate”, he continued, accusing Ardestani of sending a “report” to the building commissioner. Earlier on Wednesday, the commission heard that Nassif had become suspicious of Toplace contractors after a report about apartment defects had been passed on to Chandler.
In the call, Ardestani responded, “which report you talking about, sir?”, subsequently requesting a face-to-face meeting with Nassif.
“You can’t see me. You’re a fucking lying cunt. Bye,” Nassif ended the call.
Maheswaran was taken to messages between Ardestani and Nassif after a subsequent meeting between the two men, in which Ardestani wrote that “purpose of this meeting was to get my mate, the builder, to come and fix the issues that the building commissioner requested to be fixed”.
Maheswaran accepted counsel assisting, Peggy Dwyer’s suggestion there was “nothing threatening about that”. She put it to him that this was “clearly a request for payment so that remediation works can take place on Jean Nassif’s building”.
He rejected this, saying it was inconsistent with an audio recording of the meeting, which the commission is expected to hear on Thursday.
The commission heard that Maheswaran had already met with Chandler about the alleged extortion attempt, with the building commissioner suggesting they go to the police. Chandler himself subsequently reported it to his departmental head, and was cleared by an internal audit.
Asked why he did not share details of the people allegedly involved in the extortion attempt with Chandler, Maheswaran said he did not think it was relevant.
“Mr Nassif was taking this very, very seriously, was contemplating paying $5m to these people and from my perspective this was obviously not something that was real.”
“The best way to dispel that illusion in Mr Nassif’s mind [was] to raise it with the commissioner with whom we had a good relationship”.
Dwyer later said: “I’m suggesting to you, I want to put it straight, that you dishonestly conveyed to Mr Chandler that there had been a genuine extortion or shakedown attempt from an anonymous person,” he s

deduped_items.title: A ‘grubby rumour’ and a $5m extortion attempt: former Toplace executive gives Icac evidence
deduped_items.summary: Sharangan Maheswaran also told inquiry his bid for story on unsubstantiated rumour about then-Liberal minister David Elliott was ‘not a serious offer’Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updatesGet our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcastA purported $5m extortion attempt of fugitive property developer Jean Nassif was actually a genuine request for his company Toplace to pay a contractor, a lawyer assisting the New South Wales anti-corruption watchdog has argued.Former To
deduped_items.body_text:
A purported $5m extortion attempt of fugitive property developer Jean Nassif was actually a genuine request for his company Toplace to pay a contractor, a lawyer assisting the New South Wales anti-corruption watchdog has argued.
Former Toplace lawyer and executive Sharangan Maheswaran told the Independent Commission Against Corruption (Icac) on Wednesday he had not “dishonestly conveyed” to the building commissioner, David Chandler, that someone had attempted to extort Nassif on Chandler’s behalf.
Icac is investigating the allegation that Liberal figures Christian Ellis, Jeremy Greenwood and Charles Perrottet took $2m in illegal donations from Nassif or Toplace in exchange for political outcomes.
Greenwood and Perrottet have denied payments were for political outcomes. Ellis has moved overseas and is not expected to give evidence. Nassif, in an appearance from his Beirut bedroom, insisted he was “not corrupt”. Maheswaran, who is named in a separate allegation by Icac, has denied any wrongdoing.
The alleged outcomes include damage to the political career of Liberal minister, David Elliott, who had opposed Toplace developments, and the removal of the building commissioner, David Chandler, who had been scrutinising defects in Toplace apartments.
The commission has previously heard that Nassif claimed two individuals had asked him for $5m on Chandler’s behalf to lift prohibition orders on Toplace developments. Maheswaran subsequently passed on details of the alleged extortion attempt to Charles Perrottet.
Chandler is not named as a person of interest in Icac’s allegations and is not accused of any wrongdoing.
On Wednesday, the commission heard a phone call recorded by Nassif with one of the alleged individuals, contractor Navid Ardestani, who is not named in Icac’s allegations and is not accused of any wrongdoing.
“Navid mate,” Nassif began the call. “I didn’t know you were so fucking powerful, mate”, he continued, accusing Ardestani of sending a “report” to the building commissioner. Earlier on Wednesday, the commission heard that Nassif had become suspicious of Toplace contractors after a report about apartment defects had been passed on to Chandler.
In the call, Ardestani responded, “which report you talking about, sir?”, subsequently requesting a face-to-face meeting with Nassif.
“You can’t see me. You’re a fucking lying cunt. Bye,” Nassif ended the call.
Maheswaran was taken to messages between Ardestani and Nassif after a subsequent meeting between the two men, in which Ardestani wrote that “purpose of this meeting was to get my mate, the builder, to come and fix the issues that the building commissioner requested to be fixed”.
Maheswaran accepted counsel assisting, Peggy Dwyer’s suggestion there was “nothing threatening about that”. She put it to him that this was “clearly a request for payment so that remediation works can take place on Jean Nassif’s building”.
He rejected this, saying it was inconsistent with an audio recording of the meeting, which the commission is expected to hear on Thursday.
The commission heard that Maheswaran had already met with Chandler about the alleged extortion attempt, with the building commissioner suggesting they go to the police. Chandler himself subsequently reported it to his departmental head, and was cleared by an internal audit.
Asked why he did not share details of the people allegedly involved in the extortion attempt with Chandler, Maheswaran said he did not think it was relevant.
“Mr Nassif was taking this very, very seriously, was contemplating paying $5m to these people and from my perspective this was obviously not something that was real.”
“The best way to dispel that illusion in Mr Nassif’s mind [was] to raise it with the commissioner with whom we had a good relationship”.
Dwyer later said: “I’m suggesting to you, I want to put it straight, that you dishonestly conveyed to Mr Chandler that there had been a genuine extortion or shakedown attempt from an anonymous person,” he s

deduped_items.title: Permanent resident who sexually interfered with girl, 15, aimed to dodge deportation
deduped_items.summary: ‘Such a sentence would be neither fit nor proportionate,’ ruled the judge, who sentenced the man to more than double the time he asked for — 15 months behind bars, plus three years of probation
deduped_items.body_text:
Permanent resident who sexually interfered with girl, 15, aimed to dodge deportation
‘Such a sentence would be neither fit nor proportionate,’ ruled the judge, who sentenced the man to more than double the time he asked for — 15 months behind bars, plus three years of probation
A Hamilton, Ont., man who followed a 15-year-old down a dark trail just before midnight, grabbed her by the hair from behind, then showed her an explicit video and exposed himself has failed to convince a judge to tailor his sentence so he can avoid deportation.
Harpreet Singh, 30, was convicted in the Ontario Court of Justice for sexual interference, making sexually explicit material available to a child for the purpose of facilitating sexual interference, and exposure to a person under the age of 16 years for a sexual purpose. The permanent Canadian resident, who was born and raised in Punjab, India, argued unsuccessfully for 182 days in jail followed by two years of probation.
“Mr. Singh, a permanent resident of Canada, asks the court to impose a sentence that would preserve his right to appeal a deportation order arising from his convictions,” Justice Joe Patrick Paul Fiorucci said in his Sept. 15 decision.
“I find that such a sentence would be neither fit nor proportionate.”
Instead, the judge sentenced Singh to more than double that: 15 months behind bars, followed by three years of probation.
Reducing Singh’s “sentence to 182 days would materially understate both the gravity of the offence and the offender’s moral culpability,” said the judge.
“Such a sentence would fail to adequately reflect the seriousness of the offence, the significant harm suffered by the victim, and Parliament’s direction that denunciation and deterrence receive primary emphasis in cases involving the sexual abuse of children.”
Fiorucci accepted that Singh faces potentially significant immigration consequences. “However, those consequences do not justify reducing the sentence to a level that would otherwise be demonstrably unfit. While immigration consequences are entitled to serious consideration, they cannot be permitted to dominate the sentencing exercise or create a separate sentencing regime for offenders facing possible removal from Canada.”
The court heard that Singh sat across from the teenage girl on May 1, 2023, as they travelled on the same city bus.
“During the ride, Mr. Singh watched a sexually explicit video on his phone,” according to the decision.
The two — who were strangers to each other — both got off at the bus at the same location at 11:23 p.m.
“He followed her onto a dark trail, grabbed her by the collar (and hair) from behind, then moved in front of her holding his erect penis in one hand and his phone in the other while displaying the sexually explicit video to her,” said the decision.
The teen, whose identity is protected by a publication ban, elbowed and pushed Singh away, then fled.
She “describes the offences as humiliating, terrifying, and deeply violating,” said the decision. “She states that they fundamentally altered her sense of safety and security within her community. Before the offences, she felt comfortable travelling independently and using public transit. Following the offences, she experienced anxiety, panic, and fear in places that had previously provided her with a sense of comfort and familiarity.”
Singh’s immigration lawyer wrote to the court, explaining “that a sentence of six months (183 days) or more on any individual count would have significant immigration consequences. In particular, Mr. Singh would lose the right to appeal a removal order to the Immigration Appeal Division and would thereby lose the opportunity to seek discretionary relief on humanitarian and compassionate grounds.”
The Crown was asking for 12 to 15 months of imprisonment and three years of probation.
The judge “considered the potential immigration consequences that may flow” from the sentence he handed Singh.
The circumstances of Singh’s offences are “high

deduped_items.body_text:
Finanzas públicas sanas que permitan sostener los avances sociales. Con esta frase presentó el Gobierno de México el Paquete Económico para el año 2027.
La frase es clave para entender el momento que vivimos. Durante décadas, la presentación del citado paquete económico despertaba el interés de calificadoras internacionales y de expertos de distintos ámbitos.
Hoy, las mayorías, las mexicanas y los mexicanos de a pie, saben que tienen un gobierno empeñado en sostener el bienestar de todas y todos más allá de los buenos números macroeconómicos.
Desde el pasado que remite al “error de diciembre” y otros desastres, pretenden venir a dar lecciones, aunque ninguno de quienes estuvieron al frente de las finanzas públicas en el periodo neoliberal pueda decir, como puede hacerlo la Cuarta Transformación, que en los últimos años 13 y medio millones de personas dejaron las filas de la pobreza. Tampoco, claro, que, como ocurre hoy, la pobreza laboral se encuentra en su nivel más bajo desde que iniciaron los registros.
El propósito explícito de la estrategia gubernamental es que tengamos finanzas públicas sanas, sostenibles en el largo plazo, para mantener los avances sociales, como ha ocurrido desde finales de 2018.
Se trata de apoyar a las familias y de apoyar a quienes generan empleo, del bienestar compartido, como ha dicho la presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum. Más de un billón de pesos van a los Programas del Bienestar, un monto histórico que beneficia a millones de familias y va de la mano del desarrollo económico y de finanzas públicas sanas, a partir de ejes muy claros.
La meta establecida por las autoridades hacendarias es un crecimiento económico de más de 2% (un rango de 1.5 a 2.5%), para fortalecer la generación de empleos y el bienestar de las familias mexicanas.
El Paquete Económico protege las prioridades de la Transformación, en primerísimo lugar los Programas del Bienestar, además de garantizar la inversión pública y las participaciones crecientes a las entidades federativas. Todo, sin descuidar las obligaciones financieras del Estado mexicano.
En lo que toca a los ingresos, plantea medidas importantes para combatir a las factureras, así como la evasión y la elusión fiscal. Más eficiencia en la recaudación sin aumento de impuestos.
El cuadro se complementa necesariamente con un gasto más eficiente y con medidas para avanzar en la austeridad republicana, así como con la reducción paulatina y responsable del déficit público (de 4.1 a 3.9%).
Igualmente, se prevé un crecimiento muy importante de los ingresos tributarios, de 5.9% en términos reales, así como de los no tributarios, incluyendo los ingresos petroleros.
Las metas abarcan un aumento en el gasto neto total de 0.7%, con un aumento en el gasto programable de 1%; y en el gasto no programable, que incluye el servicio financiero del país, con un manejo muy eficiente y contenido de 0.2%.
Todo lo anterior se va a ver reflejado en un balance primario de 0.5% del Producto Interno Bruto superior al que ya estamos logrando para el cierre del 2026 de 0.1%, lo cual va a traducirse en una reducción paulatina, muy importante, del déficit público a 3.9%, que a su vez va a producir una trayectoria de la deuda estable hasta el 2030.
La SHCP ha solicitado contratar 1 billón 480 mil millones de pesos de financiamientos, para complementar los ingresos presupuestarios y financiar el Presupuesto de Egresos que analizamos en la Cámara de Diputados. Con este nuevo financiamiento, la deuda neta del sector público se ubicaría en 20 billones 774 mil millones de pesos, equivalentes al 55.8% del PIB.
Algunos analistas señalan que el monto de la deuda ha llegado a un nivel crítico y que, por lo tanto, sería muy importante reducir en mucho mayor medida el balance presupuestal para, por lo menos, mantener el nivel de deuda como proporción del PIB. Indudablemente, esto sería deseable; sin embargo, un menor endeudamiento obligaría a recortar el gasto público.

deduped_items.body_text:
Finanzas públicas sanas que permitan sostener los avances sociales. Con esta frase presentó el Gobierno de México el Paquete Económico para el año 2027.
La frase es clave para entender el momento que vivimos. Durante décadas, la presentación del citado paquete económico despertaba el interés de calificadoras internacionales y de expertos de distintos ámbitos.
Hoy, las mayorías, las mexicanas y los mexicanos de a pie, saben que tienen un gobierno empeñado en sostener el bienestar de todas y todos más allá de los buenos números macroeconómicos.
Desde el pasado que remite al “error de diciembre” y otros desastres, pretenden venir a dar lecciones, aunque ninguno de quienes estuvieron al frente de las finanzas públicas en el periodo neoliberal pueda decir, como puede hacerlo la Cuarta Transformación, que en los últimos años 13 y medio millones de personas dejaron las filas de la pobreza. Tampoco, claro, que, como ocurre hoy, la pobreza laboral se encuentra en su nivel más bajo desde que iniciaron los registros.
El propósito explícito de la estrategia gubernamental es que tengamos finanzas públicas sanas, sostenibles en el largo plazo, para mantener los avances sociales, como ha ocurrido desde finales de 2018.
Se trata de apoyar a las familias y de apoyar a quienes generan empleo, del bienestar compartido, como ha dicho la presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum. Más de un billón de pesos van a los Programas del Bienestar, un monto histórico que beneficia a millones de familias y va de la mano del desarrollo económico y de finanzas públicas sanas, a partir de ejes muy claros.
La meta establecida por las autoridades hacendarias es un crecimiento económico de más de 2% (un rango de 1.5 a 2.5%), para fortalecer la generación de empleos y el bienestar de las familias mexicanas.
El Paquete Económico protege las prioridades de la Transformación, en primerísimo lugar los Programas del Bienestar, además de garantizar la inversión pública y las participaciones crecientes a las entidades federativas. Todo, sin descuidar las obligaciones financieras del Estado mexicano.
En lo que toca a los ingresos, plantea medidas importantes para combatir a las factureras, así como la evasión y la elusión fiscal. Más eficiencia en la recaudación sin aumento de impuestos.
El cuadro se complementa necesariamente con un gasto más eficiente y con medidas para avanzar en la austeridad republicana, así como con la reducción paulatina y responsable del déficit público (de 4.1 a 3.9%).
Igualmente, se prevé un crecimiento muy importante de los ingresos tributarios, de 5.9% en términos reales, así como de los no tributarios, incluyendo los ingresos petroleros.
Las metas abarcan un aumento en el gasto neto total de 0.7%, con un aumento en el gasto programable de 1%; y en el gasto no programable, que incluye el servicio financiero del país, con un manejo muy eficiente y contenido de 0.2%.
Todo lo anterior se va a ver reflejado en un balance primario de 0.5% del Producto Interno Bruto superior al que ya estamos logrando para el cierre del 2026 de 0.1%, lo cual va a traducirse en una reducción paulatina, muy importante, del déficit público a 3.9%, que a su vez va a producir una trayectoria de la deuda estable hasta el 2030.
La SHCP ha solicitado contratar 1 billón 480 mil millones de pesos de financiamientos, para complementar los ingresos presupuestarios y financiar el Presupuesto de Egresos que analizamos en la Cámara de Diputados. Con este nuevo financiamiento, la deuda neta del sector público se ubicaría en 20 billones 774 mil millones de pesos, equivalentes al 55.8% del PIB.
Algunos analistas señalan que el monto de la deuda ha llegado a un nivel crítico y que, por lo tanto, sería muy importante reducir en mucho mayor medida el balance presupuestal para, por lo menos, mantener el nivel de deuda como proporción del PIB. Indudablemente, esto sería deseable; sin embargo, un menor endeudamiento obligaría a recortar el gasto público.

La frase es clave para entender el momento que vivimos. Durante décadas, la presentación del citado paquete económico despertaba el interés de calificadoras internacionales y de expertos de distintos ámbitos.
Hoy, las mayorías, las mexicanas y los mexicanos de a pie, saben que tienen un gobierno empeñado en sostener el bienestar de todas y todos más allá de los buenos números macroeconómicos.
Desde el pasado que remite al “error de diciembre” y otros desastres, pretenden venir a dar lecciones, aunque ninguno de quienes estuvieron al frente de las finanzas públicas en el periodo neoliberal pueda decir, como puede hacerlo la Cuarta Transformación, que en los últimos años 13 y medio millones de personas dejaron las filas de la pobreza. Tampoco, claro, que, como ocurre hoy, la pobreza laboral se encuentra en su nivel más bajo desde que iniciaron los registros.
El propósito explícito de la estrategia gubernamental es que tengamos finanzas públicas sanas, sostenibles en el largo plazo, para mantener los avances sociales, como ha ocurrido desde finales de 2018.
Se trata de apoyar a las familias y de apoyar a quienes generan empleo, del bienestar compartido, como ha dicho la presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum. Más de un billón de pesos van a los Programas del Bienestar, un monto histórico que beneficia a millones de familias y va de la mano del desarrollo económico y de finanzas públicas sanas, a partir de ejes muy claros.
La meta establecida por las autoridades hacendarias es un crecimiento económico de más de 2% (un rango de 1.5 a 2.5%), para fortalecer la generación de empleos y el bienestar de las familias mexicanas.
El Paquete Económico protege las prioridades de la Transformación, en primerísimo lugar los Programas del Bienestar, además de garantizar la inversión pública y las participaciones crecientes a las entidades federativas. Todo, sin descuidar las obligaciones financieras del Estado mexicano.
En lo que toca a los ingresos, plantea medidas importantes para combatir a las factureras, así como la evasión y la elusión fiscal. Más eficiencia en la recaudación sin aumento de impuestos.
El cuadro se complementa necesariamente con un gasto más eficiente y con medidas para avanzar en la austeridad republicana, así como con la reducción paulatina y responsable del déficit público (de 4.1 a 3.9%).
Igualmente, se prevé un crecimiento muy importante de los ingresos tributarios, de 5.9% en términos reales, así como de los no tributarios, incluyendo los ingresos petroleros.
Las metas abarcan un aumento en el gasto neto total de 0.7%, con un aumento en el gasto programable de 1%; y en el gasto no programable, que incluye el servicio financiero del país, con un manejo muy eficiente y contenido de 0.2%.
Todo lo anterior se va a ver reflejado en un balance primario de 0.5% del Producto Interno Bruto superior al que ya estamos logrando para el cierre del 2026 de 0.1%, lo cual va a traducirse en una reducción paulatina, muy importante, del déficit público a 3.9%, que a su vez va a producir una trayectoria de la deuda estable hasta el 2030.
La SHCP ha solicitado contratar 1 billón 480 mil millones de pesos de financiamientos, para complementar los ingresos presupuestarios y financiar el Presupuesto de Egresos que analizamos en la Cámara de Diputados. Con este nuevo financiamiento, la deuda neta del sector público se ubicaría en 20 billones 774 mil millones de pesos, equivalentes al 55.8% del PIB.
Algunos analistas señalan que el monto de la deuda ha llegado a un nivel crítico y que, por lo tanto, sería muy importante reducir en mucho mayor medida el balance presupuestal para, por lo menos, mantener el nivel de deuda como proporción del PIB. Indudablemente, esto sería deseable; sin embargo, un menor endeudamiento obligaría a recortar el gasto público.

deduped_items.title: Manel Esteller, médico español: “La longevidad no se debe empezar a trabajar a los 50 o los 60. Se debería empezar de pequeñito"
deduped_items.summary: El experto en longevidad estudió los últimos años de vida de María Branyas, una mujer que vivió hasta los 117.El 16 de septiembre publicó Historia de una Supercentenaria, un libro en el que cuenta la historia personal de ella y las claves que le permitieron alcanzar su longevidad.

deduped_items.title: What Venezuela Needs to Resist Disasters
deduped_items.summary: The June earthquakes are an opportunity to bridge the gap between current capacities and the vast body of knowledge on disaster prevention
deduped_items.body_text:
What Venezuela Needs to Resist Disasters
The June earthquakes are an opportunity to bridge the gap between current capacities and the vast body of knowledge on disaster prevention
Few events like the earthquakes that hit Venezuela this year, especially Vargas (now known as La Guaira) state, can prove that the human toll of a disaster is largely a political outcome, rather than a merely natural one.
Research consistently links earthquake mortality to the strength of State institutions, how effective its emergency response system is, how prevalent corruption is and how well it regulates building codes. Corrupt and incompetent States fail before the shaking starts, leaving buildings uninspected and codes unenforced. Then they fail again afterward, unable to mount a coherent response.
At the same time, a disaster can expose not only the vulnerabilities of buildings and communities but also the underlying inequities of society. Historian Rogelio Altez, one of the leading experts in Venezuela’s earthquake response, says that the June double earthquake was an MRI that showed “how there’s a privileged sector that is able to make decisions and another that has no protection and that is crushed, displaced and oppressed.” He added that the ruins of the earthquake are also the ruins of our society, arguing that the disaster reveals the structural vulnerability of the country.
Venezuela has had excellent geologists, geophysicists and engineers. Yet, it’s rare for their findings to fully translate into policy, and even rarer for them to become standard practice.
Altez emphasizes that the State has been “pathetically absent” and its response can only be compared (not in a directly proportional way) with the 1812 earthquake: “For example, because we were dealing with a government, like the First Republic, that was legitimate only for one segment of society, but lacked both resources and a solid institutional framework.” More than 200 years later, Venezuela deals with a State that “lacks institutionality, that has decided to be absent and to make, in each of its actions, a business out of the disaster.”
And this is not because we have been unable to learn from our disasters, or because we lack the proper expertise. We have the knowledge, and to some extent, the rules. What we need is enforcement of policies to prevent disasters and react when they happen in order to save lives and economies.
Using local knowledge
The overarching first lesson, and it’s one that has become prevalent throughout our coverage of the earthquake, is that technical knowledge has to be embedded in our decision-making processes, from prevention to planning and reconstruction. Venezuela, for decades, has had excellent geologists, geophysicists and engineers. Yet, it’s rare for their findings to fully translate into policy, and even rarer for them to become standard practice.
A key example of this is the process of seismic microzoning, an essential study because a large urban area might include an array of soil and conditions that define how an earthquake would impact each neighborhood. Geophysicist Víctor Rocabado explained that the process “divides the city into zones based on how areas with similar subsoil characteristics are expected to respond. Each zone is then assigned a specific design spectrum that indicates how a building should be designed or adapted to withstand a future earthquake. It’s a sort of seismic code by sector, rather than applying the same generic standard across the entire city.”
What needs to be done, Luraima Salazar says, is to “understand the risk of every zone and act accordingly with fortification and reconstruction and, yes, in some cases, abandonment, but with clear knowledge of the situation.”
Caracas is well known for its thorough microzoning, led by FUNVISIS and Dr. Michael Schmitz, which involved the geological, geotechnical, and geophysical characterization of the subsurface after more than 20 seismic refraction studies to estimate wave

deduped_items.body_text:
UNGA 2026 LIVE: Pezeshkian to address UN today; likely to respond to Trump’s 'annihilate Iran' remark
UNGA 2026 LIVE: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian will address UNGA today, outlining Tehran’s position on the West Asia conflict, just a day after Trump warned he could “annihilate” Iran if no peace deal is reached.

UNGA 2026 LIVE: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian will speak at the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) today in the afternoon session (local time) in New York. In his UNGA address, Pezeshkian is likely to press Iran's case over the ongoing war in West Asia and is expected to outline Tehran's position on the conflict. His comments will come after US President Donald Trump warned on Monday that he was deciding between “annihilating” the Islamic Republic and making a peace deal with them....Read More
Ahead of his departure for New York, Pezeshkian said Iran would forcefully present its position at international forums.
“We will forcefully raise Iran's positions in international forums. The issues we will raise at the United Nations are expressing the oppressed state of the Iranian nation, the crimes that have occurred, and the distrust that has been created. We went to the negotiating table several times and signed agreements, but unfortunately, the whole world saw how commitments were not fulfilled and the writings were trampled underfoot,” he said en route to the US, according to ANI.
What Trump said on Iran
Speaking from the UNGA podium, Trump warned that he could “annihilate the Islamic Republic” if no deal is reached to end the conflict.
“But I have a big decision to make. Will a deal be made with Iran that lets them rebuild and create a far greater country than it ever was before? Maybe one of the greatest in the Middle East or even the world. Or do I annihilate the Islamic Republic, and do it quickly, never giving them a chance to kill and destroy people and countries again? But I believe we'll make a deal right after the election, because it doesn't make sense for them not to,” Trump said.
Trump also said Iran was waiting to see how he performs in the US midterm election while maintaining that the election would not affect his approach to Tehran.
“They're waiting to see how I do in the midterm election. What they don't realise is that I'm not running,” the US President said.
Which country heads/representatives will speak today?
In the morning session, speakers are Syria, Latvia, Romania, Burundi, Iran, Paraguay, Czech Republic, Argentina, Estonia, Timor-Leste, Libya, Palau, Cyprus, Dominican Republic, Botswana, Ecuador, Ukraine, Bulgaria, Central African Republic, Panama and Ethiopia.
In the afternoon session, speakers are Poland, Namibia, Slovakia, Kenya, Serbia, Mozambique, Guinea, Eswatini, Honduras, Montenegro, Venezuela, Uganda, Rwanda, Spain, Andorra and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
UNGA 2026 LIVE: India reaffirms commitment to eliminate Hepatitis B, C as public health threats by 2030
UNGA 2026 LIVE: Union health secretary Punya Salila Srivastava outlined India's comprehensive, people-centred approach to tackling hepatitis at a UNGA 81 side event titled ‘Advancing Global Action to Eliminate Hepatitis’.
Speaking at the event, organised by the UN Group of Friends to Eliminate Hepatitis, Srivastava highlighted India's work across prevention, screening, diagnosis, treatment and care.

deduped_items.title: South Africa: The Continuation of Femicide in SA Is a Societal Failure
deduped_items.summary: [Daily Maverick] A woman goes out for a run, not to provoke, not to challenge, not to invite danger, but simply to enjoy the freedom of movement, exercise, and relaxation that should belong to every human being. deduped_items.title: Essex: A homecoming 32 years in the making, By Sonny Onyegbula
deduped_items.summary: I then stood up to reflect on my journey as a former international student, 32 years after…. I asked: “Madam Vice-Chancellor, as a former international student, I am encouraged by your vision for AI and your acknowledgment of our alumni’s global impact. Given the 25 per cent funding reduction over the past two years, how […] The post Essex: A homecoming 32 years in the making, By Sonny Onyegbula appeared first on Premium Times Nigeria.
deduped_items.body_text:
I then stood up to reflect on my journey as a former international student, 32 years after…. I asked: “Madam Vice-Chancellor, as a former international student, I am encouraged by your vision for AI and your acknowledgment of our alumni’s global impact. Given the 25 per cent funding reduction over the past two years, how do you plan to sustain our international reputation and improve the student experience without additional financial burdens on current and future students?”
My Essex story began in November 1994, when the British Council in Nigeria sponsored me under the auspices of the Constitutional Rights Project (CRP) to undertake a study tour of human rights centres, organisations, and civil society initiatives across the UK and Northern Ireland. This included a visit to the University of Essex, where I met the late Professor Kevin Boyle, a distinguished scholar known worldwide for his pioneering work in international human rights law.
I also had a 50-minute talk with the MA in Human Rights and LLM in International Human Rights Law students on my human rights work during a most turbulent time in Nigeria’s history – the General Sani Abacha regime. I returned in 1997 to pursue an LLM in International Human Rights Law. Since then, I have made at least six subsequent visits to the university to share my extensive United Nations field experience with students enrolled in the LLM programme and to serve as a mentor over several years.
At the Vice Chancellor’s invitation, I returned for my seventh visit on 21 September, a day divided into two meaningful parts: a guided tour of Wivenhoe Park’s diverse landscapes and participation in the Annual Meeting 2026.
We started on the acid grasslands, a fragile ecosystem protected by environmental regulations, where construction is strictly prohibited. The soil here is highly acidic, supporting an ecosystem that includes ground-nesting lapwings, burrowing rabbits, and elusive muntjac deer, which are rarely seen. We were informed that a dedicated full-time litter picker keeps the area clean, ensuring waste is correctly disposed of in strategically placed bins, and carefully collected.
The trees are remarkable. A giant sequoia, approximately 120 years old, suffered crown damage during a thunderstorm in the 1980s. Its spongy, weathered bark now serves more as a visual spectacle than usable timber. Interestingly, the UK currently has more redwoods than California, thanks to Victorian botanists inspired by Prince Albert’s admiration for these trees. Nearby, a common walnut tree displayed its textured bark resembling animal skin. At the same time, a black mulberry bore dark purple fruit, intentionally chosen by King James I to favour the white silk moth over the black variety. The Japanese Daimyo oak starts fruiting in just six years — significantly faster than the typical 50-year timeframe — while the medlar tree requires two full seasons of decay before its fruit becomes edible. Additionally, a cultivated strawberry tree, grown specifically for jam-making, adds to the botanical diversity.
One of the most historically significant trees is the Cedar of Lebanon, planted in the 1750s when Wivenhoe House was constructed. Historically, troops sat beneath its canopy while preparing for D-Day during World War II. Despite recent surveys declaring it healthy, a branch fell two months prior, underscoring the ongoing need for preservation efforts.
The oldest living organism on campus is an oak estimated to be over 850 years old. Gnarled and partly hollow, it predates both the university and historic structures like Colchester Castle. It existed before the completion of the Domesday Book in the 11th century. This ancient oak, held together by its own enduring history, still leafs out every spring, resilient and proud. The guide remarked that it has witnessed everything and remains standing because no one tried to exploit it; instead, it was left undisturbed.

This included a visit to the University of Essex, where I met the late Professor Kevin Boyle, a distinguished scholar known worldwide for his pioneering work in international human rights law.
I also had a 50-minute talk with the MA in Human Rights and LLM in International Human Rights Law students on my human rights work during a most turbulent time in Nigeria’s history – the General Sani Abacha regime. I returned in 1997 to pursue an LLM in International Human Rights Law. Since then, I have made at least six subsequent visits to the university to share my extensive United Nations field experience with students enrolled in the LLM programme and to serve as a mentor over several years.
At the Vice Chancellor’s invitation, I returned for my seventh visit on 21 September, a day divided into two meaningful parts: a guided tour of Wivenhoe Park’s diverse landscapes and participation in the Annual Meeting 2026.
We started on the acid grasslands, a fragile ecosystem protected by environmental regulations, where construction is strictly prohibited. The soil here is highly acidic, supporting an ecosystem that includes ground-nesting lapwings, burrowing rabbits, and elusive muntjac deer, which are rarely seen. We were informed that a dedicated full-time litter picker keeps the area clean, ensuring waste is correctly disposed of in strategically placed bins, and carefully collected.
The trees are remarkable. A giant sequoia, approximately 120 years old, suffered crown damage during a thunderstorm in the 1980s. Its spongy, weathered bark now serves more as a visual spectacle than usable timber. Interestingly, the UK currently has more redwoods than California, thanks to Victorian botanists inspired by Prince Albert’s admiration for these trees. Nearby, a common walnut tree displayed its textured bark resembling animal skin. At the same time, a black mulberry bore dark purple fruit, intentionally chosen by King James I to favour the white silk moth over the black variety. The Japanese Daimyo oak starts fruiting in just six years — significantly faster than the typical 50-year timeframe — while the medlar tree requires two full seasons of decay before its fruit becomes edible. Additionally, a cultivated strawberry tree, grown specifically for jam-making, adds to the botanical diversity.
One of the most historically significant trees is the Cedar of Lebanon, planted in the 1750s when Wivenhoe House was constructed. Historically, troops sat beneath its canopy while preparing for D-Day during World War II. Despite recent surveys declaring it healthy, a branch fell two months prior, underscoring the ongoing need for preservation efforts.
The oldest living organism on campus is an oak estimated to be over 850 years old. Gnarled and partly hollow, it predates both the university and historic structures like Colchester Castle. It existed before the completion of the Domesday Book in the 11th century. This ancient oak, held together by its own enduring history, still leafs out every spring, resilient and proud. The guide remarked that it has witnessed everything and remains standing because no one tried to exploit it; instead, it was left undisturbed.

deduped_items.title: The Fallout of a Charlie Kirk Campus Scandal
deduped_items.summary: Students and faculty across the country were punished for their reactions to the conservative activist’s murder. A recent graduate of Texas Tech’s law school is still trying to clear her name.
deduped_items.body_text:
Last September, Ellie Fisher, a third-year law student at Texas Tech, was in her 2 P.M. seminar, Race and Racism, when another student interrupted class to announce that the conservative activist Charlie Kirk had been shot. The student described Kirk as “the guy from Turning Point.” Fisher turned to a classmate and asked, “What’s Turning Point?”
Texas Tech, which is based in Lubbock, ranks among the most politically conservative public campuses in the nation; in 2024, Donald Trump carried Lubbock County by forty points. Fisher, who is originally from San Martin, California, near Santa Cruz, was an outspoken progressive. She is just over five feet tall, with long dark hair and expressive eyes that she accentuates with paste-on lashes. As an undergraduate, she founded an N.A.A.C.P. chapter at the school, led voter-registration drives, and helped get prominent Texas Democrats, including Jasmine Crockett and Beto O’Rourke, to speak on campus. “My white family, they’re, like, ‘Oh, my God, I would’ve never moved to Texas,’ ” Fisher, who was adopted as an infant by white parents, told me. “I’m, like, ‘It’s great! There’s hella Black people out here!’ ”
She was also drawn to the cowboy culture of West Texas. In middle school, she had developed a passion for livestock—when she was seventeen, a steer she raised named Rambo won a top prize at the Santa Cruz County Fair—which ultimately led to a scholarship to study agriculture at Texas Tech. She took a meat-judging course and became a strong supporter of the Second Amendment. (She has tattoos of a handgun and the words “Enemy of the State.”) After her senior year, Fisher passed up several offers to study law on the West Coast. She aspired to be a federal public defender. Texas Tech is in a region of the state—known as the High Plains—with a severe lack of indigent legal services. “There are a million Ellie Fishers right now in San Francisco,” she told her parents. “Where they need me is Lubbock.”
At law school, Fisher, who’s now twenty-six, formed friendships with many of her conservative peers. She was close with members of the campus’s chapter of the Federalist Society, several of whom were invited to her most recent Friendsgiving party, which she called “God, Guns, Gravy, and Gobble Gobble.” (“THIS IS NOT FAKE NEWS!!!” the invitation read. “The patriots are gathering.”) “The conservatives at the law school know I poke fun at them,” she told me. “They let me do it, and they drink with me while it happens.” She added, “The main thing is respect. You’ve got to be able to talk about it. And you’ve got to be friends with people.”
On the day of Kirk’s murder, Fisher was scheduled to work in the school’s criminal-defense clinic, which enlists law students to serve as public defenders in Lubbock County. As she walked into the clinic’s offices, her phone chimed with messages and news alerts. Fisher would later say that she could only recall one Kirk quote at the time, a defense of the Second Amendment in which he said its protections were worth the cost of “some gun deaths every single year.” But, during the conservative activist’s many appearances on podcasts and college campuses, he regularly expressed views designed to offend people with Fisher’s political sensibilities, including that “there’s a war on white people in this country” and that “prowling Blacks go around for fun to go target white people.” As Fisher passed the office of Joe Stephens, who ran the clinic’s program for rural defendants, she called out, “Hey, Joe Lew!” Her voice was full of energy. “Have you heard the news?” she asked. “They shot Charlie Kirk.”
Stephens didn’t immediately recognize the name. “There’s video,” Fisher said. “It looks bad.” The clip was “all over the internet,” she continued, waving her phone. Stephens gently chided her, saying, “Don’t do that.”
Down the hall, her supervisor, a tenured professor named Patrick Metze, was in his office with two students. Metze had taught at Texas Tech for nearly two dec

deduped_items.summary: Alice Weidel lebt in einer gleichgeschlechtlichen Partnerschaft mit Kindern – ein scharfer Kontrast zum traditionellen Familienbild der AfD. Wie reagiert die Parteichefin, wenn Spitzenkandidaten wie Ulrich Siegmund ihr Lebensmodell öffentlich abwerten und Parteikollegen gegen sexuelle Minderheiten hetzen? Pauline von Pezold und Frederik Schindler analysieren einen internen Kulturkampf, in dem Weidel zunehmend ins Visier der eigenen […]
deduped_items.body_text:
Listen on
Alice Weidel lebt in einer gleichgeschlechtlichen Partnerschaft mit Kindern – ein scharfer Kontrast zum traditionellen Familienbild der AfD. Wie reagiert die Parteichefin, wenn Spitzenkandidaten wie Ulrich Siegmund ihr Lebensmodell öffentlich abwerten und Parteikollegen gegen sexuelle Minderheiten hetzen? Pauline von Pezold und Frederik Schindler analysieren einen internen Kulturkampf, in dem Weidel zunehmend ins Visier der eigenen Leute gerät.
Trotz historischer Wahlerfolge in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern und Berlin brodelt es hinter den Kulissen gewaltig. Ein brisantes internes Strategiepapier des Wahlkampfmanagers Daniel Fiß rechnet gnadenlos mit dem Spitzenkandidaten Leif-Erik Holm ab und fordert einen radikaleren Kurs. Die Recherche zeigt, wie extreme Kräfte die Gunst der Stunde nach der Wahl nutzen, um unliebsame Funktionäre aus dem Weg zu räumen.
Ein Blick nach Österreich offenbart zudem tiefe Risse im europäischen Rechtsaußen-Bündnis. FPÖ-Chef Herbert Kickl inszeniert sich plötzlich als israelfreundlich und erntet dafür heftigen Gegenwind von AfD-Politikern, die von „Schuldkult“ sprechen. Zudem ordnet die Folge eine bemerkenswerte Geschichtsumdeutung ein und klärt, warum Alice Weidel Adolf Hitler öffentlich als „Linksradikalen“ bezeichnet.
„Inside AfD“ ist der POLITICO-Podcast über die umstrittenste Partei des Landes. Trotz Radikalisierung und Beobachtung durch den Verfassungsschutz wächst die AfD weiter. Wie ist das möglich? Was treibt ihre Anhänger, Strategen und Gegner an? Wie funktioniert das Innenleben der Partei? Und was bedeutet ihr Aufstieg für das politische System Deutschlands?
Antworten liefern immer mittwochs Pauline von Pezold von POLITICO und Frederik Schindler von WELT — unaufgeregt, aber kritisch.

deduped_items.title: French legal complaint says Israeli army uprooted and stole ancient olive trees from Lebanon
deduped_items.summary: French legal complaint says Israeli army uprooted and stole ancient olive trees from Lebanon Submitted by MEE staff on Wed, 09/23/2026 - 11:43 Unnamed French citizen says his family in Lebanon had cultivated the grove for 250 years before Israelis arrives A Lebanese soldier stands guard at the entrance to Zawtar al-Gharbiyeh, one of three southern Lebanese villages designated as a 'pilot zone' under an Israel-Lebanon framework agreement (Giovanna Vial/MEE) Off A war crimes complaint has been fil
deduped_items.body_text:
French legal complaint says Israeli army uprooted and stole ancient olive trees from Lebanon
A war crimes complaint has been filed in France against the Israeli army over its uprooting of a historic olive grove in Lebanon.
An unnamed French businessman, aged 37, filed the complaint, claiming that soldiers uprooted trees that were 600-years-old on his family's land in the village of Zawtar el-Charqiye, his lawyers told the AFP News agency.
The civil suit accuses the Israeli army of theft and destruction of property, which constitute war crimes.
According to the businessman, the Israeli army also destroyed his family's home in an air strike in April.
He said that no one in his family had any ties to Hezbollah, which has been at war with Israel since October 2023, and that his family had cultivated the land where the grove sat for more than 250 years.

"There is no evidence to suggest that Hezbollah was using the house or the agricultural fields as military equipment," the court filing says.
"These acts are part of the broader context of ethnic cleansing and the destruction of numerous villages by Israel in southern Lebanon," lawyers Vincent Brengarth, William Bourdon, and Nicolas Busin told AFP.
"Our client expects the French justice system to do everything possible to identify and prosecute those responsible."
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said in an i24 interview that his intention from October 7 was ultimately to wage war with Iran and expand its operations into Gaza, Syria and Lebanon.
Netanyahu said he believed on October 8 that Israel would “change the face of the… pic.twitter.com/rCqTpUmGiY
According to Lebanon's health ministry, Israeli attacks have killed 8,920 people and injured 30,595 others since October 2023.
Israeli forces remain deployed in a self-declared buffer zone extending about 10km into southern Lebanon. Amnesty International said in June that the zone covered approximately six percent of the country.

deduped_items.title: Why China’s Silicon Valley won’t need American degrees
deduped_items.summary: For nearly a century, American global power has rested on a three-legged tripod: unmatched military firepower, the ubiquitous sovereignty of the US dollar and the intellectual dominance of its higher-education system. While aircraft carriers project hard power and Wall Street manages global capital, the American university system has quietly manufactured the “soft power,” technological breakthroughs […] The post Why China’s Silicon Valley won’t need American degrees appeared first on Asia Times.
deduped_items.body_text:
For nearly a century, American global power has rested on a three-legged tripod: unmatched military firepower, the ubiquitous sovereignty of the US dollar and the intellectual dominance of its higher-education system.
While aircraft carriers project hard power and Wall Street manages global capital, the American university system has quietly manufactured the “soft power,” technological breakthroughs and elite talent required to keep the empire running.
Yet, tectonic shifts rarely announce themselves with a trumpet blast; they begin as subtle disruptions in the data. In the 2026 Nature Index, Harvard University — which had comfortably held the global top spot in scientific output since the index was created in 2014 — fell to third place. More striking still was the scenery surrounding it: nine of the top ten research institutions in the world are now Chinese.
For prominent public intellectuals like Fareed Zakaria, who has spent decades on his CNN GPS show, in columns in The Washington Post and in his landmark book “In Defense of a Liberal Education” arguing that American academic preeminence is essentially unrivaled, this shift should serve as an alarm bell.
Zakaria is quick to credit the perpetual dominance of American education with a well-worn list of structural merits such as top rankings internationally, an inherent capacity for recruiting talent from around the world, plentiful government and private research funds, an integrated approach to liberal and applied science subjects and an environment which encourages innovation and discovery rather than mere memorization.
In recent years, he has added a cautionary coda to his thesis, warning that hyper-politicization, culture-war battles, budget cuts and restrictive visa policies could cripple this delicate ecosystem.
While Zakaria’s diagnosis of current American strengths is accurate, his prognosis for the future reads more like wishful thinking than cold-eyed realism. His fatal oversight lies not in what he observes inside the campus gates, but in what he ignores outside of them to the factory gate.
Zakaria correctly maps the dimensions of American hard and soft power, yet fails to grasp the seismic economic transformations reorganizing the wider world. Academic dominance is not something the US easily achieves through the liberal way of life; it is simply a consequence of its industrial domination in the past.
As manufacturing moves from west to east, academic dominance will follow. Over the next decade, American higher education risks losing its historic leadership in science, technology, engineering, mathematics, management and financial technology.
Unless dramatic changes occur, American universities may find their global domain restricted largely to the humanities and social sciences — fields like English literature, Western philosophy, mass media, film studies and sociology.
Universities do not operate in a vacuum of pure intellectuality. Universities have been engineered to produce specific types of knowledge, and their worth has been measured by how efficiently they run the machinery of industry.
To understand why China is mounting such a formidable challenge, one must look at the historical nexus between the factory floor and the lecture hall. The world-class stature of American universities in the mid-20th century did not happen by accident; it was bankrolled and sustained by the massive industrial output of post-World War II America.
When a nation controls the world’s primary production lines, its universities naturally become the nerve centers for applied science, industrial engineering, operational management, and commercial finance.
Today, that industrial center of gravity has moved. China now accounts for roughly 37% of global manufacturing output and controls nearly 40% of advanced technology production and trade.

deduped_items.title: Why China’s Silicon Valley won’t need American degrees
deduped_items.summary: For nearly a century, American global power has rested on a three-legged tripod: unmatched military firepower, the ubiquitous sovereignty of the US dollar and the intellectual dominance of its higher-education system. While aircraft carriers project hard power and Wall Street manages global capital, the American university system has quietly manufactured the “soft power,” technological breakthroughs […] The post Why China’s Silicon Valley won’t need American degrees appeared first on Asia Times.
deduped_items.body_text:
For nearly a century, American global power has rested on a three-legged tripod: unmatched military firepower, the ubiquitous sovereignty of the US dollar and the intellectual dominance of its higher-education system.
While aircraft carriers project hard power and Wall Street manages global capital, the American university system has quietly manufactured the “soft power,” technological breakthroughs and elite talent required to keep the empire running.
Yet, tectonic shifts rarely announce themselves with a trumpet blast; they begin as subtle disruptions in the data. In the 2026 Nature Index, Harvard University — which had comfortably held the global top spot in scientific output since the index was created in 2014 — fell to third place. More striking still was the scenery surrounding it: nine of the top ten research institutions in the world are now Chinese.
For prominent public intellectuals like Fareed Zakaria, who has spent decades on his CNN GPS show, in columns in The Washington Post and in his landmark book “In Defense of a Liberal Education” arguing that American academic preeminence is essentially unrivaled, this shift should serve as an alarm bell.
Zakaria is quick to credit the perpetual dominance of American education with a well-worn list of structural merits such as top rankings internationally, an inherent capacity for recruiting talent from around the world, plentiful government and private research funds, an integrated approach to liberal and applied science subjects and an environment which encourages innovation and discovery rather than mere memorization.
In recent years, he has added a cautionary coda to his thesis, warning that hyper-politicization, culture-war battles, budget cuts and restrictive visa policies could cripple this delicate ecosystem.
While Zakaria’s diagnosis of current American strengths is accurate, his prognosis for the future reads more like wishful thinking than cold-eyed realism. His fatal oversight lies not in what he observes inside the campus gates, but in what he ignores outside of them to the factory gate.
Zakaria correctly maps the dimensions of American hard and soft power, yet fails to grasp the seismic economic transformations reorganizing the wider world. Academic dominance is not something the US easily achieves through the liberal way of life; it is simply a consequence of its industrial domination in the past.
As manufacturing moves from west to east, academic dominance will follow. Over the next decade, American higher education risks losing its historic leadership in science, technology, engineering, mathematics, management and financial technology.
Unless dramatic changes occur, American universities may find their global domain restricted largely to the humanities and social sciences — fields like English literature, Western philosophy, mass media, film studies and sociology.
Universities do not operate in a vacuum of pure intellectuality. Universities have been engineered to produce specific types of knowledge, and their worth has been measured by how efficiently they run the machinery of industry.
To understand why China is mounting such a formidable challenge, one must look at the historical nexus between the factory floor and the lecture hall. The world-class stature of American universities in the mid-20th century did not happen by accident; it was bankrolled and sustained by the massive industrial output of post-World War II America.
When a nation controls the world’s primary production lines, its universities naturally become the nerve centers for applied science, industrial engineering, operational management, and commercial finance.
Today, that industrial center of gravity has moved. China now accounts for roughly 37% of global manufacturing output and controls nearly 40% of advanced technology production and trade.

deduped_items.summary: في الصحف: خطاب دونالد ترامب أمام الجمعية العامة للأمم المتحدة تحت المجهر، من تهديد إيران إلى المبالغة في الحديث عن النفط وغزة، فيما ترى صحف أمريكية وأوروبية أن الرئيس الأمريكي قدّم رؤية للعالم تقوم على القوة و«منطق المنتصر». وفي المقابل، برز خطاب إيمانويل ماكرون، خصوصاً دعوته إلى إعادة فتح المسارات الإنسانية في غزة. أزمة النفط حضرت بقوة أيضا: فاينانشيال تايمز تكشف عن تحالف أمريكي خليجي يسعى لشراء أصول «لوك أويل» الروسية، بينما تحذر الصحف الفرنسية من صدمة وقود تاريخية تضغط على القدرة الشرائية وتض

deduped_items.summary: Representatives from charitable organizations active in the French capital reflect on the significance of the Pope’s upcoming visit to the Maison Bakhita Center for Social Support and Integration. They speak of philosophical “cafés” bringing together the homeless and women free to express themselves, of building “horizontal” relationships where everyone stands as equals, and of a piece of advice from Pope Francis that they hold close to their hearts: “Remain small.” Read all
